Sports.content:
Those in charge of Formula 1 have allowed its new rules to turn racing into a ‘battle of the bots’, says @RedPill:

I felt there was going to be some trust and proper direction within FIA and Liberty Media who owns the rights to F1 to make sure the quality of (human) racing was going to remain high quality. Boy, we were wrong. The whole debacle and agreed verbiage in contacts allowed the power unit manufacturers and investors to pretty much be the ones to dictate what was going to be allowed in F1, while retaining huge powers in the wording to prevent changes.

Fans, drivers, teams, FIA and Liberty Media are now stuck with it. I hate how the drivers are more passengers in their own cars while racing. Yes, there’s too much going in the cars, that the drivers can’t possibly manage everything and race in full anger, but this is no secret or anything new. The powers that be needed to craft specifications that used the latest tech, but still retain the drivers’ ability to fully race the car, the way a race car driver is suppose to race. That is why we watch the races.

We come and watch these F1 races because there’s humans in control of brilliant machinery, racing them to the ninth degree, but there’s a limit. If I wanted to watch automated machinery duke it out and see battle of bots I would instead go to robot contests, not F1.

Red Pill (@RedPill)

Sports.title: Teremoana Teremoana Crushes DeAndre Savage in Two
Sports.content:
In the first round, Teremoana had Savage on the defense the entire round. In the second round midway a right from Teremoana on the temple and down went Savage taking the full count on a knee from Referee Phil Austin.

In the co-Main Event Middle Michael ‘Pretty Boy’ Zerafa, 35-5 (23), #158 ¾, of Melbourne, AUST, stopped Alejandro ‘El Venado’ Ortiz, 26-2 (25), #158 ¾, of Catia, Caracas, VZ, 25-2 (24), after 9 rounds of a scheduled 10 rounds.

In the first two rounds, Zerafa had an edge using his jab. In the third round, Ortiz landed several left hooks to the chin as Zerafa countered well. In the fourth Zerafa had a good round scoring well.

In the fifth round, Ortiz landed a big right on the chin halfway through the round taking the round. In the sixth round, Zerafa came back well out landing Ortiz. In ninth round Zerafa had Ortiz hurt in an over whelming round with Ortiz struggling to the corner at the end. His corner called a halt,

Referee Paul Tapley

Fly Jasmine Parr, 9-2 (3), #112, of Gold Coast, Queensland, AUST, defeated ‘The Black Sheep’ Jemma Peart, 9-2 (3), #111 ¾, of Gold Coast, Queensland, AUST, 8×2 rounds.

In the first three rounds Parr had an edge out landing Peart. In the fourth round, Peart may have had an edge using her jab.

In the fifth and sixth rounds, Parr turned southpaw on occasions taking both rounds. In the seventh round it was the most competitive. In the eighth and final round Parr took another round out landing Peart.

Scores 80-72 by all judges.

Referee Phil Austin

Super Middle Jack Bowen, 14-1 (11), #167 ½, of Brisbane, Queensland, AUST, stopped tough Midlifeier Dalielibieke, 10-4 (8), #167 ½, of Elrumqi, CH, @ 2:15 of the seventh of an 8.

In the second round, Bowen had an edge with an effective jab, rocking Dalielibieke with an uppercut on the chin. In the third rounds final seconds both landed hard rights to the chin. In the fourth round it was a slugfest with both landing well.

In the fifth’s midway point Bowen rocked Dalielibieke with a right uppercut on the chin of his durable opponent. In the sixth Dalielibieke may have won his first round. In the seventh Bowen landed a flurry of punches causing Referee Paul Tapley to call a halt.

Fly Lekaysha Woodbridge, 5-0 (3), #112 ¼, of Toowoomba, AUST, defeated Sothia Sitthichai, 13-6 (4), #110 ½, of Bangkok, TH, over 5×2 rounds.

Referee Paul Tapley scored 50-45.

They fought on even terms for 3 rounds but Towns couldn’t come out for fourth round.

Sports.title: Jake Paul’s MVP Signs IBF Champion Elif Turhan
Sports.content:
Turhan gives Jake Paul’s promotion another major piece at 135 pounds. Caroline Dubois holds the WBC and WBO championships, while Stephanie Han owns the WBA belt.

That leaves MVP working with fighters who control all four major lightweight titles.

Turhan punched her way into that company last December in Monte Carlo. She broke down Brazilian Olympic gold medalist Beatriz Ferreira and forced a fifth-round stoppage to seize the IBF crown, registering the defining victory of her professional career.

She has since strengthened her position with wins over Taylah Gentzen in January and Gabriella Tellez in June.

Turhan brings pressure and finishing instinct to a division loaded with potential championship fights. She likes to close the distance, force exchanges and punish opponents once her combinations begin finding the target.

The Istanbul fighter becomes the first Turkish boxer to join MVP and follows Nicolson as the second addition produced by the promotion’s agreement with Matchroom.

Turhan believes the partnership can push her toward more championship opportunities.

“I am incredibly excited to be part of this powerful collaboration. This marks a major signal of the exciting initiatives we will undertake for women’s boxing globally, and I am deeply honored to be involved in this journey with all my strength and energy.”

Her next opponent has yet to be confirmed, but her ambitions reach beyond defending the IBF belt.

“I am excited for the opportunities that will come my way as I look to win more major World Titles.”

That pursuit creates an obvious pressure point at lightweight. Dubois controls two belts, Han holds another and Turhan carries the IBF championship.

If MVP eventually matches its lightweight champions, Turhan will have to establish her pressure against fighters capable of controlling distance, countering her entries and punishing her on the way inside.

Sports.title: Teremoana vs. DeAndre Savage Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Teremoana Teremoana improved to 12-0 with a second-round knockout of DeAndre Savage after another destructive heavyweight finish. Savage survived the opening round despite absorbing several heavy shots as Teremoana began finding his distance and opening up. That resistance ended quickly in the second. Teremoana cracked Savage with a big punch that buckled the American’s legs but left him standing. The Australian kept hunting the finish, dropped Savage moments later, and watched as he failed to beat the referee’s count. Savage became only the third opponent to take Teremoana beyond the opening round, but the extra three minutes merely delayed another knockout for the Australian heavyweight.

Michael Zerafa broke down Alejandro Ortiz for a stoppage victory on the Gold Coast after taking command in the later rounds. Zerafa began forcing Ortiz onto the back foot, then cracked him with a heavy shot in the seventh as the pressure increased. His corner demanded he keep letting his hands go while staying smart, telling him Ortiz was hurt whenever he opened up. Zerafa responded by pressing harder and keeping Ortiz under fire. The breakthrough came when Zerafa dropped Ortiz and immediately looked to close the show. Ortiz climbed off the canvas but remained hurt, and the fight was stopped soon afterward when he had taken enough. The victory gave Zerafa the result he needed after entering the fight under pressure and facing questions over his recent form.

Sports.title: Jack Dempsey’s Harry Wills Problem Never Went Away
Sports.content:
Following Jack Johnson’s 1910 victory over Jim Jeffries, racial violence erupted across the United States. The possibility of another Black heavyweight challenging a white champion encountered resistance from promoters, regulators, and others concerned about another interracial title fight.

Wills paid heavily for that environment.

A Dempsey-Wills fight nearly materialized in 1922 when promoter Tex Rickard selected a date and had tickets printed for a proposed bout in New Jersey. The promotion collapsed when the financing needed to meet Dempsey’s guarantee failed.

Another attempt ran into opposition in New York, where athletic commission chairman William Muldoon resisted an interracial heavyweight championship fight over concerns about racial unrest.

Dempsey also gave his critics ammunition. He drew the color line early in his championship reign before later changing his public position. His long stretches of inactivity intensified criticism that Wills was being denied an opportunity he had earned. Yet Wills himself resisted blaming Dempsey.

“My only regret in life is that I never got a shot at Dempsey, [and] I’m sure I could have beaten him,” Wills later said. “It wasn’t Jack’s fault. He wasn’t scared of anyone. He was a great fighter.”

Dempsey lost the heavyweight championship to Gene Tunney in 1926. Wills never fought for the world title.

The missing fight should count when Dempsey’s championship reign is evaluated. Wills was precisely the type of challenger a champion needed to defeat to remove questions about his dominance.

Placing the entire responsibility on Dempsey, however, ignores the racial barriers, regulators, promoters and failed financing that repeatedly interfered with the fight.

More than a century later, nobody knows what would have happened if Jack Dempsey and Harry Wills had finally met. That unanswered question is why Wills remains an unavoidable part of Dempsey’s legacy.

Sports.title: Teofimo Sr. Dismisses Shakur Stevenson’s Vacant-Belt Championships
Sports.content:
“This fight is about Teofimo Lopez trying to get the world title again, become a real three-division world champion. No vacant belts,” Lopez Sr. said to Fighthype. “Shakur got like two vacant belts, right? So, to me, he’s not a real three-division world champion. My son is going to do it the right way. We’re going to go straight to the champion. No vacant belt.”

Stevenson has actually won world titles across four divisions. His first came against Joet Gonzalez for the vacant WBO featherweight belt in 2019. He then stopped reigning WBO junior lightweight champion Jamel Herring in 2021 before defeating Edwin De Los Santos for the vacant WBC lightweight title in November 2023.

The fourth belt is difficult for Lopez Sr. to dismiss under his own standard. Shakur took the WBO light welterweight title from Teofimo in January, giving him two divisional championships won by defeating reigning titleholders.

Lopez Sr. also criticized Shakur’s fighting style and questioned how much further Stevenson can climb through the weight classes.

“I would love to fight him again. Let’s hope that we can get him before we move up too high,” Lopez Sr. said. “I don’t think Shakur can go up in the weight divisions. He’s too chinny. He doesn’t like to get hit. He’s a boring fighter.”

He believes Teofimo fought the wrong fight against Shakur. In his view, Teofimo should have boxed from the back foot instead of following the southpaw to his right all night.

Sports.title: Liam Paro Answers Devin Haney’s IBF Call
Sports.content:
“Have the WBO.. I want the IBF,” Devin said on X.

Haney seems to have signaled his preferred opponent without directly naming him. The choice makes sense. Paro brings a large following in Australia and the potential for a PPV event built around two welterweight champions.

That separates Paro from Jack Catterall, another opponent who has been discussed for Haney. Catterall presents a difficult fight with his movement, defense, timing and awkward southpaw style.

Paro is a southpaw as well, but he’s much more willing to engage and turn fights into physical exchanges. Haney has generally performed well against aggressive fighters who come forward, giving him opportunities to box from range, counter, and tie up when they get inside.

Catterall offers a different challenge. He’s unlikely to chase Haney recklessly or provide the type of pressure that allows Haney to settle into his preferred rhythm. Taking that fight would mean accepting considerable stylistic difficulty without getting another world title in return.

Paro gives Haney the opportunity to unify the division while bringing an established Australian audience to the promotion. From Haney’s perspective, that combination makes the matchup easier to understand commercially.

Nothing has been finalized, but the exchange leaves little mystery about their interest. Both champions have publicly opened the door to putting the IBF and WBO titles together.

Sports.title: Archie Moore Silences Yvon Durelle in Montreal Rematch
Sports.content:
The rematch drew 11,555 spectators, generating a gate of $140,519 to set a Montreal boxing record. Former world heavyweight champion Jack Sharkey served as referee.

Moore, already well into his 40s, had held the light heavyweight crown since defeating Joey Maxim in December 1952. Durelle, 29, remained a leading contender after his ferocious effort in their initial meeting.

Rather than trading immediately with the heavy-handed challenger, Moore fought cautiously through the opening two rounds. His defense limited Durelle’s opportunities to land the kind of power shots that had caused so much trouble in their first fight.

Two judges had Moore in front after two rounds, while the third had the fight even.

Moore changed the fight completely in the third. A hard right hand dropped Durelle, who beat the count at seven and tried to fight back. The champion quickly closed in.

Three more knockdowns followed as Moore connected with rights and lefts. After the fourth knockdown of the round, Sharkey counted Durelle out at 2:52.

Moore had turned a rivalry born from one of the greatest scares of his championship reign into a decisive three-round knockout.

Durelle faced difficult circumstances before the fight. A boating accident left him with a back injury, and his hometown of Baie-Sainte-Anne suffered the tragic Escuminac Disaster in June, when 35 fishermen lost their lives.

Moore continued his remarkable run near the top of the sport. Durelle later challenged George Chuvalo for the Canadian heavyweight title in November 1959, losing by knockout in the 12th round.

The two rivals eventually became friends. Moore retained enormous respect for Durelle, remembering him as one of the hardest punchers and toughest opponents he faced.

Their first fight became the classic. On August 12, 1959, Moore made the rematch his answer.

Sports.title: Teofimo: Turki Alalshikh Pushed Benn, Ryan Garcia Wanted Me
Sports.content:
“Conor and Ryan are fighting because it’s a Turki thing. Turki pushed that fight,” Teofimo said to Fighthype. “It wasn’t something that Ryan wanted. Ryan wanted to fight me, but, you know, it’s a business at the same time.”

Ryan has since named Lopez among the opponents he wants to face after Benn, along with Rolando Romero and Shakur Stevenson. That shows the interest is there, although it doesn’t establish how close Garcia and Lopez were to actually fighting.

Teofimo has his own fight to win first. He challenges WBA welterweight champion Romero on August 22 in Las Vegas, attempting to capture a title in a third weight division.

Wins by Garcia and Lopez would leave both operating at 147 pounds with a marketable fight available between them. Teofimo would also own the WBA belt, giving Garcia another reason to pursue the matchup.

Garcia has mentioned Romero as a possible opponent as well, meaning Rolly could put himself in position for a rematch if he defeats Lopez.

Lopez believes money and promotional relationships are increasingly determining which fights get made.

“Everybody’s right now more on the money side,” Lopez said. “Everybody’s associated with somebody. Takeover is on his own with his own.”

Teofimo is coming off his January loss to Shakur Stevenson and will be making his welterweight debut against Romero. Rolly already owns a decision victory over Garcia, giving Teofimo a chance to strengthen his case for a Garcia fight with an impressive performance on August 22.

Ghana News.title: Traders fume over demolition of Enchi market to pave way for 24-Hour Economy market
Ghana News.content:
Traders at Enchi in the Aowin Municipality of the Western North Region have expressed anger and frustration following the demolition of the Enchi market by the Aowin Municipal Assembly to make way for a new 24-hour economy market.

The demolition, carried out days ago, has left several traders without shops, stalls, and designated spaces to continue their businesses.

Some of the affected traders say they have operated at the market for years and are now struggling to determine where to relocate their businesses.

They claim the Assembly did not adequately engage them or provide an alternative trading location before the demolition.

According to the traders, the situation has disrupted their livelihoods, with some losing structures and other investments they had made in their businesses.

The concerns were raised during a visit to the demolished market by the Member of Parliament for Aowin, Oscar Ofori Larbi, who inspected the extent of the demolition and interacted with affected traders.

The traders appealed to the authorities to urgently provide an alternative space where they can resume trading while construction of the new market continues.

The MP acknowledged the concerns raised by the traders and assured them that he would engage the Aowin Municipal Assembly on the need to provide a suitable temporary location.

He said the affected traders must be considered as the 24-hour economy project progresses, stressing the need to prevent the development from leaving them without a means of livelihood.

The traders are now waiting for the Assembly to provide a concrete alternative as work on the proposed 24-hour economy market gets underway.

Ghana News.title: CUTS urges parliament to bring DVLA to order on “delinquency” fees
Ghana News.content:
CUTS International, Accra, a leading public policy think tank has called on the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA) to suspend the escalating “delinquency” charges imposed on people who renew or replace a driver’s licence after its expiry date,

Under the DVLA’s Summary of Licensing and Other Activity Rates for 2026, the standard charge for renewal before expiry is GH¢127.00. The amount rises to GH¢204.25 where the licence has expired by between one day and six months.

It rises further to GH¢279.25 for seven to twelve months, GH¢315.25 for up to two years, GH¢352.25 for up to four years and GH¢404.25 beyond four years. The schedule applies similar escalating charges to the replacement of an expired licence.

CUTS considers the automatic and escalating charges unfair, opaque and open to abuse unless the DVLA identifies the exact statutory instrument and approved fee item authorising each amount.

“The DVLA must show Ghanaians the law, the approved fee schedule and the formula behind every cedi it collects as a delinquency charge. Public power must rest on law. If the Authority cannot point to a clear legal basis for each charge, it must stop collecting the money and refund affected licence holders,” said Appiah Kusi Adomako, Esq., Director, West Africa Regional Centre of CUTS International.

The Law Requires a Clearer and Fairer Approach

Regulation 46(1) of the Road Traffic Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2519) provides that a driver’s licence “may” be renewed within one month before it expires. Regulation 46(2) then deals expressly with renewal after expiry. It states that a late renewal takes effect from the earlier expiry date unless the Authority for a good cause shown, permits that the renewal should take effect from the date of the renewal.

Both revoked L.I. 2180 and the current framework (LI 2519) recognises that renewal after expiry will occur. Regulation 46(8) also creates an offence for failure to renew as prescribed and makes a person liable on summary conviction. The law says “a person who fails to renew a driver's licence as prescribed commits an offence and is liable, on summary conviction, to a fine not less than five penalty units and not more than twenty-five penalty units or a term of imprisonment of not more than thirty days or to both.” The law gives the Ghana Police to enforce this and the court to convict offenders. These provisions raise important questions about the source, scope and administration of a separate automatic “delinquency” charge at the DVLA counter.



The use of the word “may” and not “shall” is a clear reflection of the intention of the lawmakers. Failure to renew your license becomes punitive only when driving without a valid license and not when your license is expired and are caught driving. The imposition of any fine by DVLA for late renewal of a license is therefore unlawful, ultra vires and contrary to the intention of the legislator. Imposing a fine on late renewal will amount to the DVLA interpreting the LI by 2519 replacing the word “may” to mean “shall,” which is not permissible in a constitutional democracy. Unless there is no evidence that someone with an expired license was caught driving, the regulator cannot charge anyone fee for delinquency. The Ninth Schedule to the LI provides for an automated road traffic offenses. Once the law says it is an “offence” then there can be no presumption except an evidential proof that license holder continued to drive beyond the expiry date of the license.

CUTS therefore asks the DVLA to state whether the escalating charges are renewal fees duly approved under the applicable Fees and Charges legislation, administrative penalties, or some other charge. The distinction matters. If the amounts are penalties, the DVLA must explain the legal process that permits an administrative system to impose them without proof of driving during the period of expiry, without a hearing and without a finding by a court.

“CUTS is not encouraging anyone to drive with an expired licence. Driving without a valid licence must attract lawful enforcement. Our concern is different: the DVLA should not presume that every person with an expired licence continued to drive, then impose an automatic escalating charge without first establishing the legal and factual basis,” Mr. Adomako said.

Since there is no legal basis for the escalated charges, the DVLA must desist from charging people who come to their counter to replace or renew their licenses. Whilst the charges may have found it is way into the Fees and Charges Act, it does not legitimatize it since there is no legal basis for it. Accordingly, DVLA must initiate the processes to refund to everyone who paid these charges.

Expiry does not prove that a person was driving

A person may hold a Ghanaian driver’s licence without owning a vehicle or driving regularly. The person may be ill, studying, living abroad or otherwise unable to drive for a prolonged period. Expiry of the document alone does not prove that the holder drove on a public road while the licence was invalid.

Consider a Ghanaian who leaves the country for a five-year PhD programme or a work assignment. His Ghanaian licence expires while he is abroad. He does not drive on Ghanaian roads during that period. When he returns and seeks to resume driving lawfully, the DVLA’s schedule places him in the highest delinquency bracket. He is charged more because time passed, although he did not expose any Ghanaian road user to risk during his absence.

“That citizen should be encouraged to regularise his licence before returning to the road. He should not be branded delinquent and punished as though expiry itself proves unlawful driving. The system must distinguish an expired document from the separate act of driving without a valid licence,” Mr. Adomako said.

The same practical logic applies to other public documents. Many Ghanaians renew an expired passport when they next intend to travel. The state does not infer from the expiry of a passport that the holder travelled unlawfully. The DVLA should adopt a similarly evidence-based and proportionate approach, while maintaining strict enforcement against anyone found driving without a valid licence.

The label “delinquent” is misplaced

CUTS objects to the use of the term “delinquency” for every late renewal or replacement. The label suggests wrongdoing before the person’s circumstances are considered. Public institutions should use neutral language such as “renewal after expiry” and provide clear criteria for waiver, exemption or proof of non-use.

The present system also creates a risk of repeated punishment. A driver who has already been prosecuted and fined by a court for driving with an expired licence may face an additional escalating charge at renewal. The DVLA counter does not even accept a court receipt if a court has convicted one for driving with an expired license as the DVLA says the charges are system-generated.

CUTS further asks the DVLA and the Ghana Police Service to clarify their respective enforcement roles. The public must know which institution investigates driving without a valid licence, which institution initiates prosecution, and the limited circumstances in which the DVLA may impose or collect an administrative charge.

Public Institutions Must Raise Revenue Lawfully

The DVLA needs internally generated funds to deliver licensing services. That need does not remove the duty to charge only fees authorised by law, disclose them clearly and treat the public fairly. The Authority is a public regulator and service provider. Revenue generation must remain secondary to legality, road safety and public service.

CUTS is also concerned about the GH¢181.00 charge for amending a licence holder’s electronic records. Charging people to update an address or telephone number discourages accurate records. Current contact and residential information support road safety, identity verification, criminal investigations and emergency communication. The DVLA should make basic updates to contact details free or charge only a small, cost-based amount where a new physical card is required.

“The DVLA should design fees to support compliance, not discourage it. When a citizen wants to correct an address or telephone number, the Authority gains better data. Charging GH¢181.00 for a basic update risks leaving the database outdated and weakens the public interest the database is meant to serve,” Mr. Adomako said.

CUTS calls on Parliament to conduct an urgent inquiry into the legality, approval and administration of the DVLA’s escalating “delinquency” charges and operations.

Ghana News.title: I resigned from my office job to pursue music – Perez Musik
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian gospel musician Perez Musik has disclosed that he resigned from his job at GHOne TV to pursue a career in music.

Speaking on The Career Trail on Joy Learning TV and JoyNews, he said he joined GHOne TV after completing his studies at NAFTI and undertaking his national service at the station, which was then owned by Chatterhouse.

He was subsequently employed by the station, where he worked in production, editing and directing.

During his time there, he also produced a Christian programme called Shades, which featured gospel musicians.

Perez Musik said he had put his own music ambitions aside for some time while working at the station, but eventually reached a point where he felt he needed to pursue his own talent.

“Then, Charlie, one day, the thing just tore from my eye top. I was like, ‘I'm not going to do it again. I want to go and sit at home fully and focus on my music.’ So impromptu, I just resigned,” he said.

He said the decision was influenced by the feeling that he was spending his time helping another business grow while neglecting his own creative abilities.

“I was just walking to the office. And then the voice was like, ‘You are leaving your talent and your gift. You're going to serve in another man's business to aid his business growth. It's not a bad thing. But for how long can you continue doing that?’” he recalled.

The decision was not easy, according to Perez Musik, who said he had been influenced by a book that encouraged people to remove their safety nets when pursuing their ambitions.

“That time, I had read a book. And it spoke about burning bridges, you know. If you really want to achieve something, burn all bridges, put pressure on yourself. It was difficult. It was a difficult decision. But I took it,” he said.

His resignation did not immediately lead to success. However, Perez Musik said he does not regret leaving the job.

He also expressed gratitude to Chatterhouse for the opportunities he received during his time there.

“I have no regrets about leaving my office job. But I am so grateful to Chatterhouse because they gave me a lot of opportunities that helped me along my music journey,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Farmer appeals for poultry processing plant in Asene Manso Akroso
Ghana News.content:
An agripreneur in the Asene Manso Akroso District of the Eastern Region, Edward Ansah, has appealed to the government to establish a poultry processing plant in the district to address marketing challenges facing local poultry farmers.

He said the facility would provide a ready market for farmers, improve the poultry value chain, and make poultry farming more attractive to the youth.

Mr Ansah, a beneficiary of the Nkoko Nkitinkiti initiative through the Asene Manso Agric Department of the District Assembly, is currently brooding 15,000 birds under intensive management at G.F. Farms at Manso.

He was selected for the initiative due to his continued efforts in crop production and his ability to produce poultry feed from farm produce.

Speaking to the media at Manso, Mr Ansah identified marketing as one of the major challenges confronting poultry farmers in the district.

He said consumers often preferred processed poultry meat from cold stores to live birds, making it difficult for farmers to sell their produce.

“Marketing is difficult because consumers prefer the already prepared meat at the cold stores to the live chickens,” he said.

Mr Ansah, therefore, called on the government to provide the district with a poultry processing and distribution facility to create a sustainable market for locally produced poultry.

According to him, the facility would also encourage more young people to venture into poultry farming and help address unemployment in the area.

Mr Ansah said investment in poultry processing should be prioritised alongside initiatives aimed at increasing local poultry production to help reduce the country’s high broiler import bill.

“The processing plant should be the major matching investment to recommend for the Government to sustain the Nkoko Nkitinkiti initiative,” he said.

He expressed appreciation to the government for supporting poultry farmers through the Poultry Intensification Scheme and the Ministry of Food and Agriculture under the Feed Ghana Programme and the West Africa Food System Resilience Programme.

He said the support, including grants for the procurement of equipment, feed, vaccines, and certified seeds, as well as technical training through seminars and workshops, had helped improve farmers’ operations.

Mr Ansah, however, appealed to the government to ensure the timely payment of grants to enable beneficiaries to plan effectively and sustain their farming activities.

He added that establishing a poultry processing facility in the district would complement existing government interventions and strengthen the poultry value chain from production through to processing and distribution.

Ghana News.title: Why ORAL cases? – Former Deputy AG quizzes over seeming selectivity in legal vacation hearings
Ghana News.content:
Former Deputy Attorney General Alfred Tuah-Yeboah has questioned the basis for selecting only Operation Recover All Loot (ORAL) cases for substantive hearings during the legal vacation.

His comments come amid growing debate over a directive by Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie for selected high-profile criminal cases to continue during the legal vacation.

Mr Tuah-Yeboah questioned why lawyers were not adequately involved in decisions to determine which substantive matters should proceed during the period.

He argued that lawyers and judges have an established practice of suspending substantive hearings during the legal vacation, except in circumstances where there are compelling reasons to proceed.

“If the lawyers were involved, I can assure you, perhaps the reasons that may be offered may to some extent be acceptable to the lawyers,” he said.

He cited situations where continuing a case during the vacation could be justified. "For example, there is a witness who is undergoing presentation. The witness is very old and sick, and if we risk that the matter be adjourned into October, it’s possible the person may even pass away. Any reasonable man will say, yes, in view of this, can we hear the matter in vacation?” he explained.

However, the former Deputy AG questioned why similar consideration could not be extended to the thousands of other cases pending before the High Court, particularly civil matters.

He pointed to cases involving injunctions over properties, where parties may have to wait several months before their matters are heard after the legal vacation.

“That's why the issue of selectivity has been very paramount. So why the ORAL cases, as the Deputy AG wanted to believe?” he questioned.

Mr Tuah-Yeboah also cautioned lawyers against accepting the current arrangement simply because it may benefit them in particular cases, warning that a precedent established today could have wider implications for legal practice in the future.

“Today you may think that it suits you, and so lawyers should be rushed to hear the matter whether they like it or not during legal vacations. But you don't know what will happen tomorrow. We must be very, very careful,” he said.

He further questioned whether lawyers had previously been compelled to appear in court to defend clients in substantive cases during the legal vacation.

The lawyer said that in his 24 years of practice, he had never been compelled to do so. He noted that he had handled murder cases involving jury trials and that, even when proceedings were in the middle of a trial as the legal year approached, judges traditionally adjourned such cases into the new legal year.

According to him, this practice could sometimes create significant difficulties, particularly where a juror dies during the vacation and the trial has to begin afresh.

“If in July trial, say, one of the jurors dies, you have to start the case de novo,” he explained.

Mr Tuah-Yeboah therefore argued that if substantive hearings are to be introduced during the legal vacation, the practice should be applied consistently across the judiciary rather than selectively.

“If you are introducing the system, then it must be across the board,” he said.

He challenged authorities to establish whether all judges who have been issued with warrants to sit during the vacation would be conducting substantive hearings.

“The CJ may want to say all judges with warrants can hear their substantive matters. You conduct your investigations throughout the country and find out whether all the judges with the warrants throughout the country will conduct substantive matters,” he stated.

According to him, the fact that only two specialised courts are expected to conduct substantive hearings during the vacation is what has fuelled concerns about selectivity.

“It's only two courts which are going to conduct hearings in substantive matters. And that is the reason why people are talking about selectivity,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Africa unites in Accra to forge unified climate strategy ahead of COP31
Ghana News.content:
The African Group of Negotiators (AGN) on Climate Change has officially opened its 2nd Strategy Meeting of the year, gathering the continent's top negotiators and leadership to sharpen Africa's collective position ahead of the upcoming COP31 summit in Antalya, Türkiye.

The three-day meeting, held from August 12–14, 2026, aims to move beyond a mere review of previous technical talks in Bonn (SB64) and instead establish a high-level political and technical strategy.

Addressing the assembly, AGN Chair Nana Dr Antwi-Boasiako Amoah emphasised the urgency of the moment, noting that the continent must be fully prepared before arriving in Antalya this November.

"With less than four months to COP31, we cannot afford to approach Antalya without clarity on what Africa seeks to achieve," Dr Amoah stated during his welcome address.

He urged delegates to move beyond "business as usual" and be more strategic in both substance and process.

The discussions in Accra cover a vast array of critical issues, including adaptation, climate finance, just transition, agriculture, and the Global Stocktake.

However, Dr Amoah reminded the negotiators that the stakes extend far beyond the meeting rooms.

"For our countries, the negotiations are therefore not merely about text, paragraphs or procedural decisions," the Chair remarked. "They are about our people, our economies and our development prospects".

He highlighted the lived realities of African citizens, from farmers facing unpredictable rainfall to communities suffering from drought, flooding, and coastal erosion.

A Call for Continental Unity

A central theme of the Accra meeting is the necessity of a unified African front in an increasingly complex international landscape where climate talks now intersect with trade, energy, and peace and security.

"Our greatest strength has always been our ability to come together as one African Group," Dr. Amoah said. "We represent different countries, circumstances and perspectives, but when we enter the negotiations, we carry a collective responsibility to defend and advance the interests of our continent".

The primary output of the meeting will be a practical roadmap and a "COP31 Action Matrix," which will define specific responsibilities, timelines, and expected deliverables for the months leading up to the summit.

Dr Amoah was clear that the meeting must yield tangible results: "We are not only in Accra to engage in another talking exercise… We must leave Accra with concrete outcomes and clear directions on next steps".

Beyond COP31, the strategy is also intended to lay the foundation for COP32, which is set to be hosted in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

This provides an opportunity to strengthen African leadership within the global climate process for 2027 and beyond.

The meeting is supported by various partners, including the Africa Centre for Energy Policy (ACEP), the African Union Commission, and Power Shift Africa.

As deliberations continue, the AGN leadership remains focused on ensuring that international climate decisions do not constrain the "legitimate development aspirations" of the African continent.

Ghana News.title: Church of Pentecost sheltered 500 Ghanaians fleeing xenophobic attacks in South Africa
Ghana News.content:
The Church of Pentecost provided shelter, food and clothing to about 500 Ghanaians who fled their homes amid the latest wave of xenophobic attacks in South Africa.

The humanitarian intervention was disclosed by the Foreign Affairs Minister, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, following a meeting with the Chairman of the Church of Pentecost, Apostle Dr Eric Nyamekye, in Accra on Wednesday, August 12.

According to the Minister, the affected Ghanaians sought refuge at branches of the church in Johannesburg, Pretoria West and Kempton Park after fleeing areas affected by the attacks.

The church accommodated the 500 Ghanaians for about two months before the Government of Ghana evacuated them as part of its ongoing efforts to ensure the safety of Ghanaian nationals in South Africa.

In addition to providing accommodation, the church supplied the affected nationals with food and clothing during their stay.

The Foreign Affairs Minister said the government and the people of Ghana were grateful to the Church of Pentecost for what he described as an outstanding demonstration of compassion towards Ghanaians in distress.

He conveyed the appreciation on behalf of President John Dramani Mahama and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Church praised for humanitarian support

Mr Ablakwa also commended the Church of Pentecost for its consistent humanitarian assistance to Ghanaians facing difficulties abroad.

He cited the church's support to Ghanaians during the Russia-Ukraine conflict and the COVID-19 pandemic as examples of its wider humanitarian interventions.

The Minister said the latest support in South Africa demonstrated the important role faith-based organisations could play in complementing government efforts to protect and assist Ghanaians abroad.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Church of Pentecost have also agreed to strengthen their collaboration in providing consular assistance to Ghanaians living overseas.

The partnership is expected to benefit from the church's extensive international presence, with branches in 210 overseas territories.

Meanwhile, the government says its evacuation exercise in South Africa remains ongoing.

More than 1,600 Ghanaians have so far been brought back to Ghana safely as authorities continue efforts to evacuate nationals affected by the xenophobic attacks.

Ghana News.title: Ablakwa thanks Church of Pentecost for sheltering Ghanaians fleeing xenophobic attacks in South Africa
Ghana News.content:
Foreign Affairs Minister has expressed the government’s appreciation to the Church of Pentecost for providing shelter and humanitarian support to hundreds of Ghanaians who fled recent xenophobic attacks in South Africa.

The Minister conveyed the government’s gratitude during a meeting with the Chairman of the Church of Pentecost, Apostle Dr Eric Nyamekye, on Wednesday, August 12, in Accra.

READ ALSO: Apostle Nyamekye recalls near-death experiences during six years in South Africa

According to the Minister, branches of the church in South Africa opened their facilities as safe havens for about 500 Ghanaians who fled the latest wave of xenophobic attacks.

The affected Ghanaians were sheltered for approximately two months at Pentecost branches in Johannesburg, Pretoria West and Kempton Park before being evacuated by the Government of Ghana.

The church also provided the evacuees with food and clothing during their stay.

“On behalf of His Excellency John Mahama and the Foreign Ministry of Ghana, I conveyed our eternal gratitude to The Church of Pentecost,” the Minister said in a statement.

Church's humanitarian support

The Minister also commended the Church of Pentecost for what he described as its consistent humanitarian support for Ghanaians facing difficulties abroad.

He cited the church’s assistance to Ghanaians during the Russia-Ukraine conflict and the COVID-19 pandemic.

“The Pentecost Church in South Africa generously offered their churches as safe havens to accommodate some 500 Ghanaians who fled the latest wave of xenophobic attacks,” he said.

The Minister said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Church of Pentecost had agreed to deepen their collaboration to improve consular assistance for Ghanaians living abroad.

The proposed collaboration is expected to leverage the church’s extensive international presence, with the Church of Pentecost having branches in 210 overseas territories.

More than 1,600 Ghanaians evacuated

Meanwhile, the government is continuing with the evacuation of Ghanaians affected by the xenophobic attacks in South Africa.

The Minister said more than 1,600 Ghanaians had so far been safely brought back to Ghana as part of the ongoing evacuation exercise.

The government has assured affected nationals of continued support as efforts are made to facilitate their safe return home.

The Minister concluded by expressing gratitude to the Church of Pentecost for its support, saying: “God bless the Church of Pentecost.”

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
