World.title: Colombia declares three days of mourning after deadly earthquake
World.content:
Hundreds are dead as rescuers race to find survivors of the magnitude 7.4 quake.

Colombia has declared three days of national mourning after a powerful earthquake killed more than 200 people as rescue crews race against time to find people trapped beneath the rubble.

The government said on Wednesday that flags would be lowered to half-staff at official buildings and Colombian embassies around the world “in honour of all the dead”.

Monday’s magnitude 7.4 earthquake was the strongest to hit the country in a century. It flattened buildings and damaged roads across western Colombia. More than 100 aftershocks had been recorded by Tuesday afternoon.

The disaster is also an early test for President Abelardo de la Espriella, who took office just three days before the earthquake. The first-time president came to power after a divisive election and is now facing the first major crisis of his presidency.

Government figures put the number of injured at 2,595 and the number officially missing at 195 although civilian-run databases suggested the number of people unaccounted for could be closer to 4,000.

The search for survivors has become increasingly urgent as the disaster enters its third day. Aid agencies said the first 48 to 72 hours are generally the most critical for finding people alive beneath collapsed buildings although people can survive longer if they have access to water and food.

Crews worked through the night in some of the hardest-hit cities, including Cali, Pereira, Manizales and Quibdo. In Pereira and Cali, rescuers used cranes, search dogs and heavy machinery while volunteers formed human chains to clear debris by hand.



In Cali, entire neighbourhoods appeared flattened with piles of rubble where blocks of homes and apartment buildings once stood and cars crushed beneath concrete and fallen walls. Residents have joined firefighters in searches for survivors, digging with picks, shovels and their bare hands and stopping periodically to listen for signs of life.

But the full scale of the destruction is still unclear, particularly in rural areas where little information has been coming out.

That includes Choco near the earthquake’s epicentre and one of the poorest regions in the country. Many communities there can only be reached by boat, through the jungle or by air. The region has also long been affected by violence between armed groups, making it even harder to reach remote areas.

The earthquake has put parts of Colombia’s health system under enormous strain. Part of the Hospital Universitario del Valle in Cali collapsed, forcing doctors to move patients into a parking lot and treat some people outside.

Colombians have mobilised to help. Thousands have brought food, water and other supplies to affected neighbourhoods while long lines have formed outside blood donation centres.

De la Espriella has declared a state of emergency and promised rent subsidies for families who lost their homes.

International help has also started to arrive. The United States has announced $15.5m in emergency aid, and the State Department announced on Wednesday that following a request from de la Espriella’s government, it was deploying urban search-and-rescue technical teams from Fairfax County, Virginia, and Los Angeles County, California, to help with the search effort.

The European Union has also pledged $2.3m, while Mexico has offered hundreds of search and health workers, and El Salvador said it would send two planes carrying 100 tonnes of aid.

But for rescue crews, the immediate focus remains searching the rubble.

World.title: Is Russia’s economy cracking despite the Iran war windfall?
World.content:
A widening deficit and Ukrainian strikes are testing Russia’s economy, even as war in the Middle East lifts oil revenue.

Russia’s economy has held up longer than many expected, defying Western sanctions.

But four years into the Russia-Ukraine war, the strain is starting to bite. Growth is forecast to slow to its weakest pace since 2022. The budget deficit is widening. And Ukrainian strikes are reaching deeper into the economy.

Even so, Moscow’s pockets remain deep, with more than $300bn in accessible reserves. The US-Israel war on Iran has handed it a windfall, sending energy prices higher and boosting Moscow’s revenues.

The United States has moved to cut that off, with the US Senate backing tariffs of up to 100 percent on Russian energy buyers.

World.title: WHO chief says Trump vaccine push goes against ‘decades of evidence’
World.content:
The US health secretary has spent years saying the MMR vaccine caused autism despite no medical evidence.

Click here to share on social media

The World Health Organization (WHO) chief has accused United States President Donald Trump of ignoring “decades of evidence” with his push to overhaul US childhood vaccination policy.

The warning from WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus on Wednesday comes days after Trump signed an order calling for a rethink of school vaccine mandates and renewed calls for the split of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine into three separate doses.

Trump’s Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr has long promoted a disproven link between the MMR shot and autism.

But Tedros said the science is “unequivocal” and that “vaccines including the MMR vaccine are safe and do not cause autism”.

“Vaccination policy should be guided by rigorous, independent and transparent review of the best available science, not by political influence,” he wrote in a post on X.

“That evidence is reviewed continuously as new data emerge from across the globe,” he added.

The WHO chief also warned that “delaying vaccines or separating doses unnecessarily does not make vaccination safer and can leave children unprotected.”

Since joining the Trump administration, Kennedy has launched a sweeping review of longstanding vaccines, rewritten the childhood immunisation schedule, and slashed funding for new vaccine development.

World.title: Iran remains defiant as it vows to fight US until demands met
World.content:
Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) advisers say Iran has replaced more missiles and drones than it used, and cite falling US munition stocks.

Tehran, Iran – Shortly after meeting China’s ambassador, Iran’s new security chief left no room for doubt about Tehran’s position after nearly six months of war with the United States.

“Iran’s message is clear: The Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until the US ends the war and blockade, releases Iran’s frozen assets, and agrees to a region-wide ceasefire, including in Lebanon and Gaza,” Mohsen Rezaei said in a social media post late on Tuesday.

“Until all conditions are met, the Strait will remain closed,” added the former wartime commander-in-chief of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

His defiant message was in line with conditions emphasised by his predecessor, Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, and by newly appointed commanders as Iranian authorities maintain that they are willing and capable of continuing to stand up to their opponents in the US-Israel war on Iran.

In his first meeting as secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, Rezaei sat down with a delegation led by China’s envoy to Tehran, Cong Peiwu, on Tuesday. State media said he pushed for closer ties with China, praised its unwillingness to go along with US-backed resolutions targeting Iran at the United Nations, and said any potential deal with Oman over the Strait of Hormuz is separate from Washington.

But an arrangement with Oman, which Tehran said last week had been finalised and was awaiting confirmation at the top, still does not appear imminent, with military action continuing in the Strait of Hormuz, as well as the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandeb Strait.

A merchant ship appeared to have been hit by a projectile off the coast of Oman on Sunday night, when Rezaei’s appointment was announced. The Iran-aligned Houthis in Yemen launched their deadliest recent maritime attack on Tuesday, hitting an Egyptian-owned ship in the Red Sea in an attack that killed six people, according to the Houthis’ rival, Yemen’s internationally recognised government.



The US military reported an overnight attack on Tuesday, saying a US Navy helicopter fired two Hellfire missiles at a Panama-flagged vessel in order to enforce its naval blockade of Iran’s southern ports. This marked the 12th vessel attacked by US forces since April, and the third since the blockade resumed almost a month ago after the collapse of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) that was signed by Iran and the US in June.

With the 60-day period of the repeatedly violated MoU approaching next week, mediators such as Pakistan and Qatar have said they are continuing efforts to bring the two sides closer to a diplomatic solution.

Yet the rhetoric from Tehran has only hardened over the past week, with the IRGC indicating that it aims to take threats from the administration of US President Donald Trump, including to further strike Iran’s power plants and civilian infrastructure, more seriously.

“If Iran is threatened again, hundreds of thousands of miles of energy lines, thousands of power plants, all the American and non-American systems, and even global infrastructure connected to the internet will be exposed to threat,” IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi said on Wednesday.

“The US had about 30 to 40 war vessels in the region before the war, but today not even a single US warship is present in the Persian Gulf,” he said, adding that the declining level of key air defence missiles and precision munitions in the Pentagon’s arsenal was a “big threat” facing US decision-makers.

Mohammad Reza Naqdi, an adviser to the IRGC’s chief commander, claimed on state television on Tuesday night that the force has continued to produce more ballistic missiles and drones during the war than it has been firing across the region, relying predominantly on native know-how and capabilities.

“Even if the war takes several years, our ballistic missiles would still descend on our enemies,” he said.

Military integration

In appointing six new figures to leading military posts this week, Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei consolidated a small circle of trusted officials, including longtime ally Hossein Taeb as the new head of the paramilitary Basij force of the IRGC.

Khamenei also selected Ali Abdollahi, head of the Khatam al-Anbiya joint wartime command, to lead the General Staff of Armed Forces.

Abdollahi is tasked with integrating the Khatam headquarters, which was formed during the eight-year war with Iraq in the 1980s to coordinate operations between the then-nascent IRGC and Iran’s regular army, with the general staff overseeing all armed personnel.

In his post-appointment message, Abdollahi emphasised upgrading capabilities across missiles, drones, naval, ground, cyber and asymmetric warfare, in addition to closer inter-service coordination and naval readiness to take action around the Strait of Hormuz.



IRGC commander-in-chief Ahmad Vahidi said he would cooperate with the other military leaders in order to resist the “Zionist-American arrogance”.

Battling an exacerbating economic crunch, President Masoud Pezeshkian suggested on Wednesday that the opponents of the Islamic Republic may be looking to defeat it by banking on another round of nationwide protests on the back of public discontent.

“The current war is more complex than before, and the enemy is pursuing collapse from inside the country,” he said during a speech.

Ali Akbar Javidan, head of the police border guard in the western province of Kurdistan in Iran, said on Wednesday that US claims that Iraq-based separatist Kurdish fighters could potentially launch a ground assault on Iranian soil were “delusional”.

“The country’s borders are fully safe and impenetrable through the vigilance of border personnel and the backing of people living in border areas, including the brave people of Kurdistan, Sistan and Baluchistan, and Khuzestan,” he was quoted as saying by state media.

In the meantime, most of Iran’s population of about 90 million people continues to weather the worsening impact of war and uncertainty, as well as a tightening security grip at home.

“I have given up on predicting what’s going to happen,” Jamshid, a 36-year-old resident of central Tehran, told Al Jazeera.

“I don’t expect anything to get better this year, or maybe even next year,” he said. “I just hope this situation doesn’t last a lot longer than that, because most of our youth is already gone dealing with these things.”

World.title: US consumer inflation slows in July as energy prices briefly retreat
World.content:
United States consumer inflation has slowed in July amid a short retreat in energy prices and hopes that the Strait of Hormuz would reopen.

Shipping continues to be severely disrupted since Iran established a maritime “toll booth” in the strait shortly after the US and Israel launched a war against the country in late February.

Consumer inflation rose by 0.1 percent compared with this time last month but was 3.4 percent higher than this time a year ago, according to data released by the Department of Labor’s Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) on Wednesday.

Inflation has been largely driven by fuel prices, which, despite a temporary reprieve, are rising. While energy prices declined 1.5 percent from this time last month, they are up 14.7 percent for the year.

“Energy prices have gone down in July because people thought perhaps the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz would end, but it didn’t. If you look at the past 12 months, energy prices are now much higher than they were a year ago,” Michael Klein, professor of international economic affairs at The Fletcher School at Tufts University, told Al Jazeera.

Brent crude fell 7 percent last week but has jumped this week as hopes that the Strait of Hormuz would reopen faded. Brent crude oil futures rose 0.3 percent to $89.19 per barrel on Wednesday.

Petrol prices dropped 2.9 percent from last month but surged 39.1 percent from a year ago.

At the petrol pump, prices are rising after tumbling 9 cents last week.

The average price for a gallon (3.78 litres) of petrol is $4.03, according to the American Automobile Association (AAA), which tracks daily petrol prices. By comparison, it was $4.00 on Monday, $4.08 this time last week, $3.87 a month ago, and $2.98 per gallon on February 28 , when the US and Israel first struck Iran.



Food prices rose marginally in July by 0.1 percent for the month but were 3 percent higher than this time last year.

Growing economic pressures

The inflation comes amid a lacklustre jobs report last week, where the US economy lost 23,000 jobs, with most losses in retail trade, local government (particularly in education), and hospitality, while healthcare made gains, according to the BLS.

Days earlier, the Jobs and Labor Turnover Report (JOLTS), also from the BLS, showed little change in the number of people leaving their jobs for new ones, continuing a so-called low-fire, low-hire environment.

These combined factors have put pressure on the Federal Reserve as it gauges the path forward to reach its goal of 2 percent inflation. In July, the central bank kept interest rates at 3.50–3.75 percent.

Economists are divided on whether rates will rise or remain unchanged during the next policy meeting slated for September 16, which would be the third under the new chairman, Kevin Warsh, who took over from Jerome Powell in May.

CME FedWatch, a tool that tracks the likelihood of monetary policy decisions, forecasts a 61.6 percent chance of maintaining rates, while 38.4 percent believe that rates will increase to 3.75–4.00 percent.

US markets are responding. The tech-heavy Nasdaq is up 0.7 percent, the S&P 500 rose by 0.3 percent, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average is 0.05 percent higher since the market opened.

Gold prices, which are generally considered a safe investment during times of economic uncertainty, are up by 1.4 percent to $4,428 an ounce.

The inflationary pressures are overshadowed by the upcoming midterm elections. There are only two more inflation reports before the election.

Meanwhile, Americans are divided on which party is better suited to handle the economy. Slightly more Americans, or 37 percent, believe that Democrats are better at handling the economy, as opposed to 36 percent who believe that Republicans are, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll released last week.

World.title: As Strait of Hormuz transit drops, Trump again says US has ‘control’
World.content:
Just eight vessels crossed strait on Tuesday, down from 130 to 140 prior to the war as peace talks stall.

United States President Donald Trump has doubled down on claims the United States maintains “total control” over the Strait of Hormuz, even as transit through the arterial waterway fell to a one-week low amid the US-Israel war with Iran.

Trump made the statement in a Truth Social post on Wednesday, reiterating a similar claim he made to reporters the day before as diplomatic efforts to end the conflict and fully re-open the strait have continued to stall.

“The U.S.A. has total control over the Strait of Hormuz. I THINK WE WILL KEEP IT!” Trump said.

He went on to claim the ongoing US blockade of Iranian ports “is being called, by everyone, “A WALL OF STEEL,” and there is nothing Iran can do about it”.

“Iran is all talk and no action, the Bully of the Middle East No Longer,” Trump said, ending his message with, “Praise be to Allah!”

Despite the statement, Iran has continued to assert its influence over the strait as it has pursued talks with Oman on future management. Wider peace talks with the US have been largely paused amid the Iran-Oman talks, which do not include Washington.

Iran has said it will not allow full traffic in the strait until the US naval blockade is lifted, sanctions are lifted, and its assets are unfrozen.

While ships can still transit through the strait, they face several obstacles and heightened threats. That has caused the volume of traffic to drop dramatically.

Reuters news agency reported that just eight ships transited through the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, far below the 130 to 140 ships pre-war rate. That was down from the previous ten-day average of about 12 ships, according to trade analytics platform Kpler data.

The US and Israel launched the war with Iran on February 28. The US and Iran signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) aimed at ending the conflict in June, but the agreement dissolved in mid July with both sides renewing attacks.



Fighting between the US and Israel has been mostly in recent days, with sporadic incidents. That included a US Navy military helicopter striking a Panama-flagged cargo vessel on Tuesday.

The Yemen-based Houthis have also opened a new front in the war, with attacks on vessels in the Bab al-Mandab Strait. Six people were killed in a Houthi attack on an Egyptian-owned ship on Tuesday, in the first deaths from such an attack.

Stalled peace efforts

Speaking on Wednesday, Pakistan’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Tahir Andrabi, said Islamabad was working to “bring the two parties to the negotiating table” and prevent efforts to undermine the peace process.

He added that Pakistan’s deputy prime minister and deputy foreign minister held talks with officials from Iran, Saudi Arabia and Kuwait on August 10, and that Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi is also visiting Tehran.

Despite the lack of progress, the Trump administration has continually signalled its desire for an off-ramp in the war, which remains politically unpopular in the US ahead of midterm elections in November.

Some analysts saw Trump’s latest statements as part of a concerted effort to frame the conflict as a victory, despite falling short of stated goals of ending Iran’s nuclear programme, ending its influence in the region and fomenting wider regime change.

“Unfortunately, the determination to demonstrate that the United States is ‘winning’ at all costs is creating a virtual reality that prevents both the administration and the president from making decisions based on the actual situation on the ground,” Dennis Citrinowicz, a senior researcher at the Institute for National Security Studies, wrote in a post on X.

“The United States does not control the Strait of Hormuz. Despite everything that has happened, Iran retains sufficient capabilities to disrupt maritime traffic through the strait,” he added.

Others have questioned US Energy Secretary Chris Wright’s statement on Tuesday that “the seven-day average for oil leaving the Strait of Hormuz is currently up to almost 9 million barrels per day”. Wright said that, when combined with upgraded land delivery infrastructure, fossil fuel deliveries from the region were close to pre-war levels.

In a post on X, Brett Erickson, an analyst at Obsidian Risk Advisors, said there is “zero evidence that 9Mbpd is exiting the Strait of Hormuz per day”.

“Zero. Not ‘maybe’, not ‘potentially’,” he added.

World.title: Lebanon passes long-sought amnesty law, a day after death penalty repeal
World.content:
The legislation will ‘exceptionally’ reduce certain prison terms, says Lebanon’s parliament speaker.

Lebanon’s parliament has approved a general amnesty law that is expected to benefit thousands of convicted prisoners, detainees and wanted people.

The legislation passed Wednesday in a “show-of-hands vote”, reported Lebanon’s official National News Agency. It is the first law of its kind since 1991.

The office of the country’s parliament speaker said the law would “exceptionally” reduce certain prison terms.

Long demanded by numerous Lebanese political factions, the amnesty law aims to reduce overcrowding in prisons, where many inmates await trial for years.

However, it has faced backlash from some family members of Lebanese soldiers and servicemen killed in attacks, who fear the perpetrators could receive undue leniency.

Lebanese authorities did not immediately announce the number of people who would be freed or receive reduced sentences under the law, which comes a day after Lebanon’s parliament also formally abolished the death penalty.

According to Imad al-Hout, one of the lawmakers in favour of the bill, the law reduced the sentences of those facing death and life imprisonment to 17 “prison years”.

That is equivalent to 12 years and nine months of actual imprisonment in Lebanon, where a prison year is calculated as nine months.

The law also calls for the release of inmates in ongoing trials who have been detained for more than 12 prison years without charges.

In its 2025 report, the country’s National Human Rights Commission said that prisons had an overcrowding rate of 300 percent, with prison authorities reporting at least 6,268 inmates by the end of March.



‘Long-awaited’

A push for general amnesty grew after the 2024 fall of longtime Syrian president Bashar al-Assad, as Lebanon jailed many prisoners over events linked to the Syrian civil war.

Most of those prisoners hail from northern Lebanon’s Sunni-majority city Tripoli and are accused of crimes that include attacking the Lebanese army, participating in clashes and planning bombings.

Other political forces, including the Iran-backed Shia movement Hezbollah, have been demanding amnesty for their communities.

Thousands of families from the eastern Baalbek and Hermel regions, bastions of Hezbollah and its ally Amal, where illicit cannabis cultivation is widespread, have been demanding amnesty for drug-related offences and car theft for years.

Christian parties, meanwhile, pushed for an amnesty law to include the families of those who joined an Israeli-backed group and fled to Israel after its withdrawal from southern Lebanon in 2000, fearing reprisals, particularly from Hezbollah and its supporters.

Deputy Walid Baarini praised the “long-awaited passage” of the amnesty law and expressed hope it would mark “a new chapter” that brings justice “to those who deserve it”.

“Amnesty is not forgetting a right, but rather prioritising mercy and wisdom when they align with the requirements of justice and the national interest,” he wrote in a post on X.

Lebanon previously passed a general amnesty law in the wake of its 1975-90 civil war.

World.title: Members of Trump's cabinet remained on decoy plane, after president's quiet exit
World.content:
It is also unclear what the cabinet secretaries and other officials, along with the Air Force members working on the plane, knew of the operation. Members of the press have said they were not aware that they were on a decoy flight.

Various ruses, often referred to as "shell games" by Secret Service personnel, are common.

Identical versions of the president's heavily armoured limousine, for example, often switch positions in motorcades, as do helicopters transporting the president in the air.

More elaborate operations often take place during high-risk trips abroad, afnd in those cases reporters on Air Force One are typically briefed and asked not to report the movements in real-time.

In March 2000, for example, then-President Bill Clinton flew to the Pakistani capital of Islamabad on an unmarked executive jet that landed after a decoy jet with the livery of Air Force One.

Ahead of the trip, the White House informed USA Today reporter Susan Page - then the head of the White House Correspondent's Association - of the security arrangements.

"They told me about the extraordinary security procedures being taken because of the dangers flying there, including the use of the decoy plane," Page revealed for the first time this week.

"Of course, the dangers threatened the journalists covering the trip as well as President Clinton," she said in an interview with the Washington Post.

It is also not currently clear what, if any, danger the occupants of the plane carrying Rubio, Bessent, other staff and the White House press pool were in during the Ankara trip.

The White House Correspondent's Association has not publicly commented on the incident.

World.title: Israeli settlers besieging Palestinian families in West Bank village
World.content:
Israeli settlers have been besieging two Palestinian families in their homes in the occupied West Bank since Sunday, with the families saying their supplies were running out and rights groups urging the authorities to step in.

On Wednesday Israeli security forces were reported to have withdrawn from the Jewish settler outpost in the village of Qusra near Nablus, following clashes with a crowd of extremist settlers. About a dozen settlers are said to remain at the site.

After the Palestinian homeowners made their initial report to the Israeli army, the first soldiers who arrived at the scene were filmed praying with the settlers.

The Abu Ridi and Hassan families have been posting on social media appealing for help after their water and power supplies were cut off and their food stocks ran low.

It is not clear exactly what the settlers in Qusra want. In the past, settlers have forced Palestinians out of their homes and seized their properties.

The stated aim of the settlers is to empty the area of its Palestinian residents.

The latest developments come as a top UN official told the Security Council in New York on Tuesday that "the West Bank is at breaking point".

All settlements are illegal under international law. Outposts are set up without official Israeli authorisation.

Palestinian security camera footage shows settlers tearing down a wall outside the Abu Ridi family's home on Sunday evening and using the stones to block the road.

This left seven people - including two young girls â unable to leave their homes while other Palestinians could not reach them. They live in what is known as Area B, part of the West Bank under Palestinian administrative control and Israeli security control.

Posting on Facebook, Qusay Abu Ridi said the situation was critical, "especially as we are completely isolated".

He wrote: "We are living in our own home, on our own land, and we are asking for nothing more than the right to live safely and with dignity."

Aysha Hassan told Reuters the settlers had "tried to break the gate" to the house and "started throwing stones at us, cursing and insulting us".

She said her family was "dying of fear, extremely terrified".

On Monday, Israeli settlers blocked Israeli journalists from the left-leaning Haaretz newspaper from trying to reach the Palestinian properties. The reporters said Israeli soldiers at the scene refused to help them when their car was blocked for two hours. They were told the area was a closed military zone, however the order was not enforced on the settlers.

A day later the Israeli human rights group Yesh Din urgently appealed to the head of the Israeli military's Central Command for the army to protect the besieged residents, evacuate the settlers' outpost and hold the settlers accountable.

Late on Tuesday, a Palestinian ambulance was finally allowed to reach the families, delivering food and taking one child away for medical treatment.

At about the same time, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) put out a statement condemning the establishment of the new outpost. It said that entering and seizing Palestinian homes was "illegal, reprehensible, and unacceptable activity".

When the head of its Central Command, Maj Gen Avi Bluth and other senior officers arrived at the scene early on Wednesday they are said to have met residents and voiced their "grave concern".

Afterwards, Palestinian security camera video shared with the BBC showed confrontations between Israeli soldiers and border police and a large crowd of settlers. The security forces used tear gas and stun grenades.

World.title: Woman pulled alive from rubble 36 hours after Colombia quake
World.content:
A 32-year-old woman, who had been trapped under rubble for 36 hours following the 7.4-magnitude quake which shook western Colombia, has been rescued alive.

Daniela Largo was pulled from beneath a collapsed building in the city of Pereira after a 10-hour-long rescue operation.

Firefighters finally managed to reach her via a tunnel they dug below four concrete slabs under which she had been buried.

At least 188 have died in the quake, according to official figures, and hundreds remain missing.

In Pereira, a city in Colombia's coffee-growing region, 79 people are confirmed to have died, the second-highest number after Cali, where 95 are dead, according to figures by the Association of Colombian Capital Cities (Asocapitales).

Largo's mother told AFP news agency that a local resident had heard her daughter cry out for help from beneath the rubble.

Once emergency workers had arrived at the site, they were able to locate Largo with the help of a small camera.

However, her rescue was complicated by the fact that four heavy concrete slabs were blocking the way.

Local firefighters aided by colleagues deployed from the capital, BogotÃ¡, and the disaster response team of the national police force had to dig two tunnels to reach her.

Through one opening, dug from above, they were able to provide Largo with oxygen. But it was only through a second tunnel, dug from below, that they were able to free her.

Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella celebrated her rescue on social media, describing it as "news which fills us with hope".

Largo's mother said that "at home, her 12-year-old son is waiting for her".

In Pereira, at least 92 buildings collapsed. Fifteen people are known to be trapped and another 37 have been reported missing, according to Asocapitales.

In Cali, Colombia's third most populous city, more than 200 people remained trapped as of 16:00 local time on Tuesday.

World.title: LA Lakers to be sold in record $12.5bn deal
World.content:
The Los Angeles Lakers are to be sold for a reported record-breaking $12.5bn, external (Â£9.3bn) - less than a year after Mark Walter took a majority stake in the NBA franchise.

Josh Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared, and former Disney chief executive Bob Iger are buying the controlling interest in one of the world's most iconic sports teams.

Walter bought his share, reportedly worth an estimated $10bn (Â£7.45bn), from the Buss family in a deal that was unanimously approved by the NBA Board of Governors in October 2025.

Kushner and Iger said in a statement: "As lifelong NBA fans, we are deeply honoured for the opportunity to become stewards of the Los Angeles Lakers, one of the most iconic sports franchises in the world.

"We have immense respect for the leadership and vision of Jerry and Jeanie Buss.

"Our long-term commitment is to build on that foundation, compete at the highest level, and serve this extraordinary team, its fans, and the city of Los Angeles."

More to follow.

World.title: US inflation eases as food and fuel costs cool
World.content:
US prices rose 3.4% in the year to July, slightly lower than the 3.5% in the year to June, new figures show.

Energy remained volatile as the Middle East conflict has continued. While gasoline prices were down 2.9% in July compared to June, they were up 24.6% over the year.

Month to month, inflation rose 0.1%, mainly due to an increase in housing costs, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said. Even small moves in rent can lift the overall headline figure as it makes up a large share of household spending.

Food prices rose only slightly in July and at a slower rate than in June, while energy prices fell, offering some relief for consumers.

While inflation was slightly lower in July compared to June, that means prices are rising at a slower pace, not that prices overall are falling.

Prices excluding food and energy rose 0.2% after staying flat in June, with medical care and airline tickets edging higher and car insurance continuing to fall.

The new Federal Reserve chair, Kevin Warsh, has said the central bank's priority is to "keep inflation moving down" while avoiding unnecessary shocks to the economy.

In a recent press briefing, Warsh said the Fed cannot use a "magic wand" to undo years of above-target inflation and must stay patient as price growth cools gradually.

One of the Fed's key jobs is to keep inflation near 2%, a level policymakers say keeps prices stable, supports steady economic growth, and helps prevent deeper downturns.

President Donald Trump has also said inflation is still too high for many families, pointing to rent and grocery bills as signs that the cost of living remains a major concern.

Financial markets reacted calmly to the latest figures, with stocks little changed as the figures were broadly in line with market expectations.

Recent labour market concerns have also softened expectations for a rate increase, after July's report showed a loss of jobs.

World.title: Danube river's low water levels reveal remains of WWII soldiers and motorcycle
World.content:
The bodies of two World War Two German soldiers have been found in Budapest's Danube river, due to record-low water levels after an intense drought.

Found alongside their remains were the identification tags of the two soldiers, a largely intact German army Wehrmacht motorcycle, a wedding ring and a Kuban shield - a combat badge of the Wehrmacht, the German War Graves Commission said.

The remarkable finds have sparked hope that some families could finally discover the fates of their ancestors, more than 80 years on from the war.

"Now begins a puzzle, in which we will try to determine the identity of the two dead," Arne Schrader, of the German War Graves Commission, told German newspaper Bild.

The wreck in the Danube was reportedly discovered on 2 August, when a passersby reported part of the motorcycle protruding from the rocks on the riverbank in downtown Budapest.

The team also found anti-tank mines, leading to the temporary closure of the riverbank as a bomb disposal unit was deployed.

Some of the items found in the river, notably the identification tags and motorcycle, are remarkably well-preserved due to the mixture of harbour sludge and oil found on the river bed, the German War Graves Commission said.

The commission is a German non-profit organisation that searches, recovers and buries the war dead on behalf of the German government.

The motorcycle is thought to be a DKW NZ 350-1 model, the organisation said, which was produced specifically for wartime use from 1944.

The commission added that of the two tags found, one belonged to a Wehrmacht soldier, and the other to a member of the Waffen-SS, which was declared a criminal organisation responsible for war crimes at the Nuremberg Trials.

World.title: Thousands of Canadians call for US ambassador's expulsion
World.content:
More than 60,000 Canadians have signed a petition calling for the US ambassador in Ottawa to be expelled for undermining diplomatic relations between the two neighbours.

The online petition accuses Pete Hoekstra of "making repeated interventions in Canadian political discourse" and of having "normalised the Trump administration's threats to annex Canada as the '51st state'" of the US.

In a statement to the BBC, the US embassy said it was aware of the petition but declined to comment further.

Canada and the US are currently engaged in intense period of trade talks, aiming to reach an agreement before new US tariffs take effect next Wednesday.

The petition, launched by a woman in Calgary, also raises concerns about meetings in Washington between the US state department officials and some Albertans who want the province to separate from Canada.

It requests Ambassador Hoekstra be formally removed from his role, and a parliamentary committee review "U.S. diplomatic interference in Canadian domestic affairs".

A Republican and a Trump ally, Hoekstra has been a fierce defender of US President Donald Trump's trade policies, saying they are meant to secure the safety and prosperity of Americans.

He has also described the relationship between the two countries critical.

But his time in Canada has not been low key.

There was a dust-up between Hoekstra and Ontario's trade representative, and the ambassador has been criticised for reposting Trump's comments about Canada becoming the 51st state and telling reporters it would be a "great discussion to be had" , externalby the leaders of the two countries.

Most recently, he faced criticism for inviting one of the leaders of the 2022 Freedom Convoy movement to his official Fourth of July celebration.

He has also described some of the political rhetoric in Canada as "anti-American" and has frequently expressed frustration at the decision by most provinces to remove US alcohol from store shelves - a key point of friction in the current trade talks.

The petition for his recall will be tabled in parliament later this year by Green Party leader Elizabeth May. BBC has contacted May's office for comment.

The House of Commons allows for Canadians to submit petitions, and there are dozens open at any given time, many receiving just a few hundred signatures.

Once a petition, which must be submitted by a Canadian resident, is authorised by member of parliament, it is posted on parliament's website. If it reaches at least 500 valid signatures, it is then presented in the House and requires a government response.

The petition reached that bar as of Wednesday morning, garnering more than enough support to be presented in Canada's House of Commons.

It comes at a time when Canadian negotiators are working urgently to avert a planned 50% American tariff on roughly $20 billion to $28 billion in Canadian goods.

Last month, Trump announced the proposed tariffs in retaliation for what he called "unequal treatment" of US cars, dairy and alcohol.

Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney warned in response that a potential further retaliation was on the table if the new tariffs were enforced.

Canadian media have reported that an interim deal could be reached by Ottawa and Washington in the coming days.

World.title: Singapore and S Korea pull Trader Joe's seasoning over poppy seeds
World.content:
Singapore and South Korea have pulled Trader Joe's Everything But the Bagel seasoning from e-commerce platforms because it contains poppy seeds.

While they do not naturally contain opiates, poppy seeds are banned in both countries because they can get contaminated with opiates by fluid in the poppy plant during harvesting.

More than 20 online listings of the popular seasoning have been removed, Singapore's Central Narcotics Bureau said on Wednesday.

Last week, Seoul authorities said the seasoning tested positive for morphine and codeine, which are opiates found in the plant's sap.

Apart from poppy seeds, the product also contains sesame seeds, sea salt, minced garlic and minced onion. It was released by American grocery chain Trader Joe's in 2017.

Authorities in Singapore have urged anyone who has bottles of the seasoning to dispose of them.

"Singapore adopts a strict policy of zero tolerance towards controlled drugs," the narcotics bureau said, according to a CNA report.

"The possession, consumption, importation, exportation, manufacturing and trafficking of any controlled drug, even in trace amounts, is an offence under the Misuse of Drugs Act," it said.

In South Korea, investigators say some people brought the seasoning back home as souvenirs from their overseas trips before listing it for resale.

Some did so without realising it contained controlled substances, while others did so knowingly, according to a report by The Korea Herald.

"Even if a product is legally sold overseas, it may be classified as a narcotic substance or a prohibited import in Korea, so particular caution is required," a police official said.

World.title: CBN removes FX, government securities restrictions on discount window access
World.content:
The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has removed restrictions on banks’ access to its Standing Lending Facility (SLF) arising from participation in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and primary auctions of government securities.

The apex bank disclosed the changes in a circular signed by CBN’s Acting Director, Financial Markets Department, Okey Umeano, on Wednesday.

The review followed an assessment of developments and existing market practices in the foreign exchange, money, and fixed-income markets, as well as the frameworks governing access to the SLF, Tenored Repo Operations, and participation in Open Market Operations (OMO).

The apex bank said the existing restriction on institutions accessing the Discount Window from participating in OMO auctions on the same day would, however, remain in force.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Restrictions on access to the Discount Window arising from participation in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) are hereby removed,” CBN said.

It also stated that restrictions linked to participation in primary auctions of government securities had been removed.

The regulator also announced the lifting of the suspension of Tenored Repo Operations, saying the move would provide greater flexibility for liquidity management.

“The suspension of Tenored Repo Operations is hereby lifted. Accordingly, the CBN may conduct repo operations across approved tenors ranging from 4 to 90 days to support effective liquidity management, improve money market functioning and enhance monetary policy implementation,” CBN stated.

OMO participation framework

CBN further revised its OMO participation framework to allow a broader range of investors to participate in both primary and secondary OMO markets through Deposit Money Banks (DMBs).

It said eligible investors would include individuals, corporates and non-bank financial institutions, while DMBs would continue to submit bids and settle transactions on behalf of their customers.

“OMO participation (primary and secondary markets) shall be open to all eligible investors through Deposit Money Banks (DMBs). Eligible investors include individuals, corporates and non-bank financial institutions.

“DMBs shall continue to submit bids and settle transactions on behalf of their customers,” CBN said.

The apex bank added that the volume, tenor, and frequency of OMO issuances would continue to be determined by prevailing liquidity conditions and monetary policy objectives.

OMO auctions, CBN said, would also continue to use the existing single-bid auction format.

The new provisions take immediate effect, with CBN directing all banks, authorised dealers and other market participants to ensure strict compliance.

“All banks, authorised dealers and market participants are required to ensure strict compliance,” the apex bank said.

World.title: Lawmaker cautions NASS against external political influences
World.content:
The House of Representatives deputy spokesperson, Philip Agbese (LP, Benue), has cautioned lawmakers against allowing the National Assembly to be used to advance the interests of external political actors ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Mr Agbese, in a statement on Tuesday, said. However, lawmakers had legitimate concerns about the state of the country, particularly insecurity and the implementation of constituency projects; they must be careful about the motives and timing of actions taken in parliament as the elections approach.

His comments followed calls to the National Assembly to suspend its recess and resume plenary to address what they described as pressing national challenges.

A group of lawmakers under the aegis of the Save Democracy Group recently raised concerns about what it described as the “nosediving” of Nigeria’s democracy, citing alleged constitutional breaches, poor budget implementation, opaque public expenditure, economic hardship, and worsening insecurity.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The group, comprising lawmakers from different political parties and regions, made its position known in a statement issued in Abuja on 5 August.

While acknowledging his colleagues’ concerns, Mr Agbese questioned the timing of the demand that the National Assembly suspend its recess.

“One cannot say the highly respected lawmakers are wrong, but the timing is suspicious,” he said.

The lawmaker said the proximity of the 2027 elections made it necessary for members of parliament to scrutinise their actions and ensure that the legislature was not drawn into political battles being driven by interests outside the National Assembly.

“The 2027 elections are just around the corner, and one must be careful not to be seen to be running errands for highly vested political interests outside the parliament,” he said.

He urged lawmakers to ensure that legitimate parliamentary interventions were driven by national interest rather than the political calculations of individuals or groups seeking to influence the 2027 elections.

‘National Assembly isn’t a rubber stamp’

Mr Agbese also rejected the perception that the 10th National Assembly merely endorses bills and policies initiated by the executive.

He said the legislature had independently initiated several measures to address challenges facing Nigerians, arguing that the executive’s introduction of similar proposals should not automatically be taken as evidence that parliament was acting as a rubber stamp.

“The idea is that, contrary to the insinuation being created in some quarters that we pass every bill and motion from the executive, I want to clear the air that we are working ahead of the executive on bills that have a positive impact on the generality of people,” he said.

He cited the proposed establishment of state police as an example, saying the National Assembly had been working on the issue before the executive presented its own proposal.

“We have been on the state police bills for some time now. The initiative remains solely that of the Parliament,” he said.

President Bola Tinubu’s administration recently introduced an executive bill to establish a constitutional framework for state police.

Mr Agbese said the executive’s intervention should instead provide an opportunity for both arms of government to harmonise their positions and produce a stronger proposal before it is transmitted to the state Houses of Assembly.

“What the executive has done so far by introducing an executive bill is to come in at the right time for both arms of government to have a refined document at the centre before sending the same proposal to the State Houses of Assembly,” he said.

“It is just to ensure that we don’t waste taxpayers’ ₦ resources unnecessarily by going back and forth.”

Concerns over unpaid contractors

On the controversy over the non-payment of contractors handling constituency projects, Mr Agbese acknowledged that the federal government had not fulfilled its commitments to contractors who executed projects on behalf of lawmakers.

He said the issue should not be ignored, regardless of the political circumstances surrounding the debate.

“The executive has not done well on their promise to pay contractors who have used their resources to execute constituency projects for the lawmakers. It is wrong and no need to sugarcoat it,” he said.

He, however, said the leadership of the National Assembly was engaging the executive to resolve the matter rather than allowing it to become another source of confrontation between the two arms of government.

The lawmaker also invoked Mr Tinubu’s previous experience as a parliamentarian, saying the president understood the importance of maintaining a functional relationship between the executive and legislature and ensuring that approved budgets were implemented.

“He is not just an experienced parliamentarian who has served the country in that regard; Mr President understands the essence of a good and harmonious working relationship with the parliament,” he said.

Insecurity

On insecurity, Mr Agbese said the country was beginning to record gains despite ongoing attacks and other security challenges in parts of the country.

He cited the rescue of kidnapped citizens in Oriire, Oyo State, Kwara State and other locations as evidence of progress in the operations of the security agencies.

“We are beginning to record positive gains despite the numerous challenges that we are being faced with as a country,” he said.

He commended the Chief of Defence Staff, Olufemi Oluyede, and other service chiefs for what he described as a strategic approach to coordinating the armed forces.

Mr Agbese said the experience of the military leadership was important to the country’s efforts to tackle insecurity, while also commending the federal government for measures aimed at improving the welfare of military personnel.

He specifically cited the recent increase in military personnel salaries and the renovation of military barracks as measures that could improve troops’ welfare and morale.

‘The House does not take decisions without a quorum’

Mr Agbese also dismissed allegations that the House leadership routinely makes critical decisions without the required quorum.

Some people said the House leadership doesn’t allow a quorum before making critical decisions. That is not true,” he said.

He maintained that established procedures guided legislative proceedings in the House and that the institution operated a transparent process consistent with international standards.

“We run a transparent legislative process that is of international standard,” he said.

The deputy spokesperson further urged members who disagreed with decisions of the House leadership or their colleagues to use established parliamentary mechanisms rather than resorting to confrontation.

“I doubt if the parliamentarians who want to fight have any boxing experience. We can’t allow that,” he said.

World.title: Abia rolls out app to track high-risk pregnancies, set to recruit more health workers
World.content:
In its sustained effort to reduce maternal and child mortality in the state, the Abia State Government has deployed a digital application called CYTrack to identify, monitor and manage high-risk and teenage pregnancies across the state.

The Commissioner for Information, Okey Kanu, disclosed this on Monday, 10 August, while briefing journalists on the outcome of their Executive Council meeting, which was presided over by Governor Alex Otti.

This is contained in a statement issued on Tuesday by Ferdinand Ekeoma, the special adviser on media and publicity to Governor Otti.

According to the commissioner, the application, which the State Ministry of Health is piloting, has successfully tracked teenage pregnancies and monitored expectant mothers through delivery to prevent avoidable maternal and child deaths.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“This app, referred to as CYTrack, has been used to successfully track teenage pregnancies and monitor such pregnancies up to delivery to prevent maternal mortality,” Mr Kanu stated.

The commissioner added that the deployment of the technology is part of the Otti administration’s reforms in the health sector, which he noted have continued to produce measurable improvements in healthcare delivery across the state.

Mr Kanu further revealed that data from functionalised Primary Healthcare Centres (PHCs) showed increased healthcare utilisation, particularly in outpatient visits and deliveries.

According to him, “The first 50 functionalised PHCs accounted for more than 20 per cent of the 1,067,000 outpatient department visits recorded between July 2025 and June 2026.

“Three additional PHCs have been functionalised between 27 July and 7 August, bringing the total number of functionalised centres in the state to 151, up from 148.

“Another 25 equipped PHCs are scheduled for functionalisation within the next three months,” the information commissioner disclosed.

Increased enrolment in the Abia health insurance scheme

On the Abia State Health Insurance Scheme, Mr Kanu noted that between 27 July and 7 August, enrolment increased from 233,000 to 237,000.

He also disclosed that the Abiriba Community Improvement Union, North America, has committed to sponsoring over 1,000 people under the scheme.

He urged other communities and groups in the state to emulate the gesture by helping the needy and vulnerable access quality healthcare.

In line with the ongoing transformation of the health sector, Mr Kanu said the Abia State Civil Service Commission will commence another phase of recruitment of healthcare professionals. He noted that 742 medical personnel have been hired so far.

“The new exercise is targeting Medical Officers, Dental Officers and Consultants for both full-time and part-time appointments,” he said.

The commissioner said the health sector reforms under Governor Otti have attracted external recognition, citing a recent report by Philips Consulting and SBI, which ranked Abia first nationally in healthcare affordability and among the top three states in healthcare quality.

He described the recognition as independent validation of the transformation recorded in the state’s health sector.

“The ranking and recognition by Philips Consulting serves as independent validation of Abia’s impressive transformation journey so far in the health sector,” Mr Kanu noted.

Information about the new app

Contributing, the Commissioner for Health, Enoch Ogbonnaya Uche, explained that the CYTrack application was developed from a pilot project using Google technology. It captures key demographic and pregnancy information, including a woman’s age and last menstrual period. This enables health workers to identify high-risk pregnancies and determine expected delivery dates and antenatal care schedules.

He explained that teenagers, women without antenatal care, and those who rely on traditional birth attendants are among groups considered particularly vulnerable to complications during pregnancy and childbirth.

“This application sends reminders to pregnant women ahead of their antenatal appointments and, where necessary, alerts responsible adults within their communities to ensure that the women receive appropriate care.

“When we don’t see them, the app, two days before their antenatal, sends a reminder that they should come for antenatal,” Mr Uche, a medical doctor and professor, explained.

The health commissioner added that the system also enables health workers to track pregnant women approaching their expected delivery dates and arrange for them to be taken to health facilities when necessary. He noted that the system has already contributed to successful deliveries among teenage pregnancies managed through the programme.

Mr Uche said the initiative was developed to address Abia’s peculiar maternal health challenges and is being adapted to suit the state’s needs.

According to the health commissioner, the state government’s objective is not only to provide “well-equipped and adequately staffed hospitals, but also to tackle the underlying factors responsible for maternal mortality by identifying vulnerable women early and ensuring that they receive timely care.”

The commissioner, therefore, urged pregnant women to enrol in the state’s health insurance programme, noting that registered pregnant women are entitled to free maternal health services and delivery, including Caesarean section, under the Basic Health Care Provision Fund arrangement.

World.title: Over 2,700 Osun residents access free healthcare as SROL expands SegunCare to include mental health support
World.content:
Osun State, Nigeria – 8th August 2026 – More than 2,700residents in Imogbara, Odo-Ijesha and Iperindo received free healthcare during the 4th Annual Community Medical Outreach by Segilola Resources Operating Limited (SROL).

Held on the 7th and 8th August 2026, the outreach delivered essential services to host communities and marked a major milestone: the expansion of SegunCare, the company’s programme to provide long term treatment and support to community residents with noncommunicable chronic diseases,to include more comprehensive mental health support.

During the two-day outreach, residents benefited from:

● 2762 medical consultations with qualified doctors

● 81 residents scheduled for general and specialist surgical procedures

● 1860 laboratory investigations

● 563 eye examinations, 21 scheduled eye surgeries and 174 free prescription reading glasses distributed

● Screening for hypertension, diabetes, HIV, Hepatitis B & C, tuberculosis and other health conditions

● Health education and wellness sessions

● 7 chronic mental health issues identified, mental health rehabilitation and counselling

● 50 additional residents enrolled into SegunCare for ongoing management of chronic illnesses

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Building on the successful launch of SegunCare in 2025, this year’s outreach marks the next phase of the programme with the integration of more mental health support. Mental health diagnoses and treatment have always been part of SegunCare, but this year SROL deepened that support.

The expanded programme now includes counselling to help patients cope with the emotional toll of long-term diagnoses, rehabilitation support for residents affected by substance use, grassroots education campaigns to address cultural misconceptions about chronic disease and patient support groups to combat social isolation. The expansion reflects SROL’s evolving approach to community healthcare, recognising that long-term wellbeing depends on supporting both physical and mental health.

Since its introduction last year, SegunCare has continued to provide monthly medication, routine monitoring and long-term disease management for approximately 279 residents living with chronic illnesses. Following this year’s outreach, an additional 50 beneficiaries have been enrolled in the programme, ensuring that more residents continue to receive care long after the annual outreach has ended.

Speaking on the impact of this year’s programme, Dr PrincewillOsuchukwu, Medical Services Manager at SROL, said, “Our vision has always been to ensure that quality healthcare is not limited by location or affordability. While the annual outreach provides immediate access to essential medical services, we recognise that lasting health outcomes require sustained care.

Through SegunCare, we continue to support residents living with chronic illnesses long after the outreach has ended, and this year, by integrating more mental health support, we are taking another important step towards delivering more holistic healthcare for our communities.”

One of the beneficiaries of SegunCare, Adeshina Sherifat, who has continued to receive treatment through the programme since enrolling last year, described it as life changing. She said, “Before SegunCare, buying my medication every month was very difficult because I couldn’t always afford it.

Today, I receive my medication regularly, my health is monitored, and I feel much stronger. Knowing that the support continues even after the outreach has given me confidence and peace of mind. ”

Also speaking on the programme, Hon Soji Gbege, Chairman of the Iperindo Community Development Agreement (CDA) Committee, said, “For many families in our communities, quality healthcare remains expensive and sometimes out of reach. What has mattered most to us is not just what SROL provides during the outreach, but how consistently they have shown up for our communities year after year. That consistency is what has built trust between SROL and the people here, and it is what gives residents confidence that this support is not a one-time gesture.”

Since its inception, SROL’s Annual Community Medical Outreach has reached over 13,000 residents. It remains one of the company’s flagship initiatives focused on preventive care, specialist treatment, and long-term health management.

As SROL continues investing in healthcare, education, economic empowerment and infrastructure, the programme underscores the company’s commitment to creating lasting social impact beyond its mining operations.

World.title: PalmPay joins CBN’s 7th Africa Emerging Markets Forum, shares perspective on regional payment integration
World.content:
PalmPay Group (“PalmPay”), a multinational fintech company providing digital financial services across emerging markets, was honored to participate in the Central Bank of Nigeria’s 7th Africa Emerging Markets Forum (AEMF 2026), held on July 29-30, 2026, in Abuja. At the forum, Chika Nwosu, Managing Director, PalmPay Nigeria, shared his perspective on the need for greater investment in interoperable payment infrastructure to support Africa’s next phase of economic transformation.

The forum brought together policymakers, regulators, development institutions, and private sector leaders to examine how stronger regional collaboration, digital innovation, and coordinated financial systems can deepen economic integration across the continent.

Speaking on the research paper titled “Deepening Regional Economic Integration Through Cross-Border Payments, Fintech, Infrastructure, and Policy Coordination,” Nwosu highlighted that Africa’s next priority should be moving beyond financial inclusion to financial integration.

“The opportunity is no longer just connecting more people to financial services. It is connecting African markets through financial services. True regional integration means making it easier for businesses to pay suppliers, receive payments, and grow across borders with confidence.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

PalmPay also emphasized that reliability must remain at the center of Africa’s digital transformation. As payment ecosystems become increasingly interconnected, strengthening cybersecurity will be critical to sustaining growth and building confidence in digital finance. The company reaffirmed its commitment to building a safer digital financial ecosystem through continued investment in consumer education, industry partnerships, and its robust security architecture.

The company’s position aligned with broader discussions at the forum.

Central Bank of Nigeria Governor Olayemi Cardoso called for Africa to move beyond being consumers of technology and become creators of solutions designed for the continent’s specific challenges. In a LinkedIn post by the CBN, the governor also emphasized the need to unlock women’s full economic participation, noting that “Africa cannot fly with one wing.” This aligns with PalmPay’s commitment to drive inclusive finance.

In 2025, the company supported more than 3,000 women entrepreneurs in Kano and Kaduna with digital banking tools and capacity-building opportunities, while continuing to expand access to digital financial services for SMEs and other underserved communities. Reaching underserved groups is PalmPay’s core priority.

During a fireside discussion, WTO Director-General Dr. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala also urged African leaders to prioritize implementation, strengthen regional integration, and create conditions that attract greater domestic investment, noting that sustainable development begins with confidence from local investors.

For PalmPay, this reflects a broader belief: Africa’s next economic transformation will be defined not only by the agreements it signs, but also by the systems it builds.

PalmPay said it will continue to strengthen Nigeria’s payment infrastructure and work with regulators, financial institutions, and ecosystem partners to support a more connected, secure, and inclusive digital economy.

About PalmPay Group

Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Hong Kong, PalmPay Group is a multinational fintech company providing digital financial services to financially underserved, high-growth emerging markets across Africa and Asia.

PalmPay Group provides individuals and businesses with essential financial services such as payments, savings, insurance, credit, and payment acceptance tools. Where smartphone ownership is the barrier to digital finance, PalmPay finances the device itself, often giving people their first phone and first financial account at once.

The Group has been recognized by TIME, the Financial Times, CNBC, and more as one of the world’s top finance companies. Its contributions to financial inclusion have also received official acknowledgement from the central bank regulatory authorities in its core operating markets.

World.title: ‘My entire family is now on social media’ — Peller laments after wedding
World.content:
Nigerian TikToker Habeeb “Peller” Hamzat has expressed frustration over his family’s growing presence on social media, days after his wedding to fellow content creator Amadou “Jarvis” Aminata.

Speaking during a livestream on Tuesday night, the 21-year-old complained about his parents’ conduct at his white wedding and also reacted to a viral video purportedly showing his father sharing a hotel bed with another man.

Peller said the attention surrounding his family had become overwhelming, claiming that his parents and siblings had suddenly become active subjects in social media conversations.

“I don’t know what’s wrong; all my family members are now on social media. My father, mother, sisters and everybody have now turned into social media users overnight. I’m currently angry with them. I’m tired of their behaviour; they should just leave me alone,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Peller and Jarvis held their wedding ceremonies on several dates, beginning with a court and civil wedding on 29 July, followed by a traditional wedding on 1 August and a white wedding on 8 August, all in Lagos.

Wedding drama

Reflecting on the white wedding, Peller alleged that his parents disregarded his request to invite only a limited number of guests.

“During my white wedding, I told them to invite only a few people, but my mother came with her boyfriend, and my father came with his girlfriend, and turned my wedding into a party.

“A polygamous family is a very bad thing. There are extended and nuclear families, but I come from a polygamous one; my father married more than one wife, and that’s my problem.”

Father’s viral hotel video

Peller also addressed a viral video purportedly showing his father sharing a bed with another man in a hotel room, which had prompted speculation online about his father’s sexuality.

The TikToker rejected claims that his father was gay, although he said he was currently unhappy with him.

“You people who are calling my daddy gay because of the viral video of him in a hotel with a man on the same bed, how did he father me if he’s gay? I’m currently angry with him, and I’ve informed him that I’m not happy with him.

“I don’t know what’s wrong; all my family members are now on social media. My father, mother, sisters and everybody have now turned into social media users overnight. I’m currently angry with them. I’m tired of their behaviour; they should just leave me alone.”

Tanzanians and fans of the singer are calling on Priscilla, daughter of actress Iyabo Ojo, to “release” their son, using the hashtag #FreeJumaJux.

They criticised Priscilla, adding that the singer had lost significant weight since their marriage.

Priscilla, husband’s response

World.title: Why banning under-16s from social media may not be the answer — Adebayo Tijani
World.content:
Governments around the world are increasingly debating how far they should go in restricting children’s access to social media amid concerns about online safety and young people’s digital wellbeing.

Australia became the first country to implement a nationwide minimum age of 16 for accounts on certain social media platforms.

The restrictions took effect on 10 December 2025 and require age-restricted platforms to take reasonable steps to prevent under-16s from holding accounts.

One social media platform that appears to attract many young people is TikTok.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

And with mixed reactions trailing calls to restrict children’s access to social media, the likes of Adebayo Shehu Tijani have a different opinion.

He claims that being online before he turned 16 did not merely mean scrolling through social media for entertainment. It exposed him to opportunities that he says helped shape the young advocate he is today.

A seat at an unusual table

Now, years later, the Nigerian Mass Communication student and film editor has a seat at an unusual table: TikTok’s Global Youth Council, where young people from different countries contribute their experiences and perspectives to conversations about how the social media platform can be made safer and more supportive for younger users.

Mr Tijani joined the council in 2024 after applying through Praesidio Safeguarding, TikTok’s partner on the initiative, and undergoing several interviews.

According to him, his journey gives him a personal perspective on a question increasingly confronting governments, parents and technology companies around the world: should children under 16 be kept off social media altogether, or can they be protected without shutting them out of the opportunities available online?

“Speaking from my own experience, I started discovering opportunities online before I turned 16. Those experiences helped me grow as a young leader and opened doors that have shaped my journey, including serving on TikTok’s Global Youth Council. If I had not been able to access those opportunities, my path might have looked very different,” he told PREMIUM TIMES on Wednesday.

Global debate

For Mr Tijani, the safety concerns driving such debates are legitimate, but restrictions should not become the only response.

He argued that social media is no longer simply a source of entertainment for young people but also a means of learning new skills, finding opportunities, connecting with mentors, expressing themselves and building communities.

He said, “Rather than asking whether young people should or should not be on social media, I think the bigger question is how we can help them use it safely and responsibly. That is why digital education, parental involvement, and strong safety features are so important.”

Mr Tijani is also the founder of Advocate for Youth Safety and Health Initiative (AYSHI), a youth-led initiative focused on youth safety and health.

He says his membership of TikTok’s Global Youth Council has allowed him to contribute to discussions about young people’s experiences on the platform.

He said council members participate in discussions, workshops, and meetings with TikTok teams and online safety experts, where they provide feedback on issues affecting younger users.

Since joining, Mr Tijani said he has contributed feedback on digital wellbeing, privacy, reporting systems and safety tools.

He cited TikTok’s Well-being Missions, meditation feature and updates to the TikTok Teen Safety Centre among initiatives to which members of the council have contributed perspectives.

“Knowing that our input can influence real changes on a global platform is very empowering,” he said.

“It has also taught me valuable skills such as teamwork, communication, leadership, and how to advocate for young people’s needs.”

For Mr Tijani, the experience also illustrates a broader problem with conversations about children’s online safety: young people are frequently discussed. Still, they are not always included in the decisions that affect them.

“Young people are the ones using these platforms every day. We understand the opportunities they create, but we also experience the challenges firsthand,” he said.

“That lived experience is valuable and should be part of the conversation when decisions are being made.”

Digital education

Beyond giving young people a voice, Mr Tijani believes digital education should become a fundamental part of preparing children for life online.

“I believe digital education is just as important as learning subjects like Mathematics or English, because young people today spend a significant part of their lives online,” he said.

“It’s not enough to know how to use social media. Young people also need to understand how to use it safely, responsibly, and positively.”

Such education, he said, should teach young people how to protect their privacy, identify misinformation, report harmful content, respond to cyberbullying and develop healthy digital habits.

He also believes responsibility cannot be left to technology companies alone.

Parents, schools, governments, civil society organisations and technology companies, he said, all have roles to play in creating safer online environments.

What platforms can do

Mr Tijani pointed to parental controls and digital-wellbeing tools as examples of interventions that can give families greater oversight without necessarily excluding teenagers from social media.

Among the TikTok measures he highlighted are Time Away Scheduling, which allows parents to set screen-free periods, and tools that enable parents to see accounts their teenagers follow, accounts that follow them, and blocked accounts.

He also cited a wind-down feature for users under 16, which interrupts the For You feed after 10 p.m. with a full-screen reminder and calming music intended to encourage them to stop scrolling.

Mr Tijani said members of the Global Youth Council played a role in providing input into such tools.

But he argues that individual features cannot, on their own, solve the challenges young people encounter online.

And while governments continue to debate whether keeping under-16s away from social media is the best way to protect them, Mr Tijani believes safety and opportunity do not necessarily have to be competing goals.

“I believe the goal should be to create an internet where young people are both safe and empowered.”
