Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping subsequently held talks in Kazan, followed by further diplomatic efforts aimed at improving bilateral relations.

World.title: 'Has no shame': Kangana Ranaut attacks Rahul Gandhi over Amit Shah debate row, Parliament logjam
World.content:
NEW DELHI: BJP MP

on Wednesday launched a sharp attack on Lok Sabha leader of opposition

over the continuing stalemate in Parliament, accusing him of making a "mockery" of the House and the country while refusing the government's offer for a debate on the students' protest.

Ranaut alleged that Gandhi was demanding a statement from Union home minister

over the police action against protesters, while simultaneously saying the opposition would not listen to him.

"I feel he is making a mockery of the country. He constantly ridicules the nation; for him, everything is a joke. This is the first time I am seeing Parliament being made such a mockery of. In the same breath, he says, 'We want an answer from Amit Shah ji--asking whether or not he did such-and-such to the students--while simultaneously declaring, 'We are not here to listen to him'.

He has no sense of shame or propriety left," news agency ANI quoted Ranaut saying.

"The whole world is watching and wondering what kind of person this is. The way he is venting his frustration and insulting Parliament and, by extension, the entire nation and its citizens convinces me, as someone observing his role as leader of the opposition, that this will be his final term," she added.

Ranaut, who represents Mandi in the Lok Sabha, also attacked Gandhi over his political record, saying the Congress under his leadership had "lost a hundred elections" and claiming that he would not retain the leader of opposition post in the future.





"He is demanding the resignation of the Prime Minister--a democratically elected leader who has secured a massive mandate for a third consecutive term. He seems to think that no one else in this country should even exist but him. Then there are his other actions--colluding with figures like Soros or international forces to tear the country apart and leave it in ruins. Ultimately, it doesn't matter whose resignation he demands or what he wants, because the public simply doesn't care about him," she said.

World.title: Delhi Police’s ‘Kuchu Puchu’ Gen-Z twist to warn Delhiites about Chinese manjha
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

has found a rather unusual way to join the viral âkuchu-puchuâ Gen Z trend, using internet humour to deliver a serious warning about kite-flying strings.

In a recent social media post, the police urged residents to enjoy kite flying but stay away from banned Chinese manjha and plastic-coated strings, which can cause serious injuries to people and animals.

âDear Kuchu Puchu, Patang Udao but Say NO to Chinese Manjha, Samjhe?â the police wrote, giving its usual safety messaging a more playful, social media-friendly tone.

The message comes as authorities step up action against the banned string in Delhi. The Crime Branch recently seized more than 1,300 rolls of Chinese manjha during an enforcement operation. In a separate action, Central Delhi Police recovered around 120 rolls.

The post quickly drew reactions online, with some users poking fun at the police for adopting the language of Gen Z.

âGen-Z mode of Delhi Policeâ, âThey are updatingâ, some comments read. Behind the light-hearted presentation, however, is a serious safety concern.

Chinese manjha is generally made using synthetic or plastic material and can be coated with abrasive substances. Because of its sharpness, it can cause deep cuts and injuries.





It can also become particularly dangerous for birds, which can get caught in the string while flying. There have already been fatal consequences in Delhi.

Recently, a 32-year-old man travelling to Mundka for business suffered a cut to his neck after coming into contact with Chinese manjha in southwest Delhi's Uttam Nagar.

In another tragic incident in 2023, a seven-year-old girl died after being injured by Chinese manjha while travelling with her father on a scooter in west Delhi's Paschim Vihar.

The police's latest post therefore carries a straightforward message beneath all the social media humour. People can continue flying kites and enjoying the activity, but using banned synthetic strings can put lives at risk.

The campaign also reflects a broader change in the way police departments communicate with the public, with serious safety warnings increasingly being delivered through the language, trends and humour that dominate social media.

World.title: Cybersecurity at nuclear installations accorded highest priority; AERB, external govt agencies assess security at plants: Centre
World.content:
Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Chennai: The Union govt on Wednesday informed Lok Sabha that security assessments are conducted periodically at all nuclear power plant sites by the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) and âexternal govt agencies. âIn a written reply to Congress MP Manickam Tagore, minister of state in the Prime Ministerâs Office Jitendra Singh said the plants also conduct internal security assessments. âThe observations made are reviewed, monitored and necessary upgrades are carried out for compliance,â he said.Tagore had sought details of third-party security audits at nuclear plants, including Kudankulam, and measures to counter threats from drones, cyberattacks and sabotage. He asked whether any foreign or suspected state-sponsored cyberattack attempts had been detected during the past three years.The National Alliance of Anti-nuclear Movements urged the Union govt recently to constitute a commission of inquiry to investigate the alleged leak of files related to the Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant. The statement comes in the wake of a ransomware group reportedly publishing hundreds of files linked to the Kudankulam plant which are said to be highly sensitive.The govt did not directly disclose whether any such foreign or state-sponsored attempts had been detected. It said cybersecurity at nuclear installations was accorded the âhighest priorityâ, with continuous monitoring and surveillance mechanisms in place. Preventive measures include access controls, regular security audits, vulnerability assessments, incident-response mechanisms and capacity-building programmes. It cited CERT-inâs (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team) role in issuing alerts and advisories, coordinating responses to cyber incidents and operating the National Cyber Coordination Centre.On physical security, Singh said nuclear power plants were equipped with perimeter intrusion-detection systems, access controls, CCTV surveillance and X-ray baggage inspection facilities. The AERB conducts regulatory inspections covering nuclear security.Singh said regulatory-approved emergency preparedness plans were in place at every nuclear power plant, including Kudankulam. Exercises involving local administration, security agencies and plant authorities are conducted periodically, and feedback is used to revise and strengthen preparedness plans.Tabletop, Integrated Command, Control and Response (ICCR) exercises are held once every two years. Mock exercises are organised according to the National Disaster Management Authorityâs schedule. An ICCR exercise was conducted at the Kudankulam nuclear power plant on April 15, 2025.The govt said all other nuclear power plant sites had conducted their latest ICCR exercises since Sept 2024. At Kalpakkam, an off-site emergency exercise involving the district administration, was conducted on July 17, 2026, with an initiating event from the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor.

World.title: 'Got firebombed by Indians on net': Trump aide Navarro recalls backlash after Russian oil, tariff remarks
World.content:
NEW DELHI: US senior counsellor for trade and manufacturing Peter Navarro has said President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have a âvery good working relationshipâ and will resolve differences over the US tariff issue linked to Indiaâs imports of Russian oil.

Responding to an ANI question, Navarro recalled the backlash he faced in India after writing an op-ed on the India-Russia oil trade.

âDuring the Ukraine-Russia war, 6-8 months ago, I think I wrote an op-ed, which absolutely factually correctly pointed out that prior to the Russian invasion of Ukraine, India was not involved in the oil trade with Russia, but afterwards it got heavily involved and was selling a lot of refined products on behalf of Russia, which helped feed the war machine,â Navarro said.

âAnd that issue has been resolved. Maybe I had a little bit to do with that with that op-ed, but I can tell you, I got actually firebombed by the Indian continent on the internet. All I would say to you, don't do that,â he added.

Navarro, however, said the issue would ultimately be handled by Trump and Modi themselves.

âThat's not how we resolve problems here in America. With respect to your question, the President and your Prime Minister have a very good working relationship.





They are going to work that out amongst themselves, and it's not for me or any gaggle to get between that,â he said.

His remarks come amid renewed concerns in India over possible US trade measures targeting countries that continue to purchase Russian energy.

Earlier on August 7, the US Senate passed the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 by an 86-11 vote. The bipartisan legislation would give the US president discretionary authority to impose tariffs of up to 100% on goods from countries that are among the top five buyers of Russian crude oil or natural gas.

India and China remain among the largest buyers of Russian crude.

World.title: ED arrests ex-treasurer of Cong's Chhattisgarh unit in Rs 3,000 cr liquor scam
World.content:
Chhattisgarh Congress leader Ramgopal Agrawal (Photo: Agencies)

NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate has arrested Ramgopal Agarwal, former treasurer of the Congress in Chhattisgarh, in an ongoing money laundering investigation in the Rs 3,000 crore liquor scam in the state. The agency said a substantial part of the proceeds of crime, generated in cash, was delivered to Agrawal in his capacity as the then Treasurer of the Chhattisgarh Pradesh Congress Committee.Agrawal, who was lodged as an undertrial in the Central Jail, Raipur, was arrested on Tuesday and has been remanded to ED custody for seven days. He is accused of criminal conspiracy, cheating, forgery and corruption in the excise administration of Chhattisgarh during 2019 to 2023.âInvestigation revealed that a syndicate comprising Anil Tuteja (retd IAS), Anwar Dhebar and Arun Pati Tripathi (an Indian Telecom Service officer) orchestrated a large-scale scam in the stateâs liquor trade and generated proceeds of crime of Rs 3,000 crore through illegal commission on liquor sales, unaccounted country liquor sale, commission collected from distillers and from foreign liquor companies and against the grant of FL-10A licences,â ED said.The agency further said that âstatements recorded of the persons who handled and moved the cash have revealed that the cash was delivered, at the instance of Ramgopal Agrawal and through handlers of the syndicate, at Rajiv Bhawan, Raipur, the then office of the Chhattisgarh Pradesh Congress Committeeâ.Agarwal was summoned for questioning earlier, and in his statement subsequently recorded, he gave evasive replies, the agency said.

World.title: SJM calls for boycott of US brands over tariff threat
World.content:
RSS-affiliated Swadeshi Jagran Manch has called for a boycott of American products

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From Russian oil to Pepsi, Coke and social media, the Swadeshi Jagaran Manch has sought to turn the latest US tariff threat into a wider âswadeshiâ campaign, calling on Indians to boycott American products and platforms and asking the Centre to stay firm in trade negotiations with Washington.The RSS-affiliated economic body reacted to legislation passed by the US Senate that, according to SJM, would empower the American President to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries making significant purchases of Russian oil. It said the move amounted to an attempt to dictate Indiaâs energy choices.âNo country has the right to dictate Indiaâs energy security and sovereign trade policy,â SJM national co-convenor Ashwani Mahajan said, adding that Indiaâs Russian crude purchases were driven by price, availability, supply diversification and consumer interests.SJM said the proposed measure assumed greater significance with India and the US engaged in negotiations for a bilateral trade agreement, arguing that talks âcannot be conducted on gun pointâ.It also urged the Centre to reconsider two recent policy moves which it claimed favoured US companies â changes allowing FDI e-commerce entities greater flexibility over inventory for exports and an amendment enabling merchant discount rate on certain UPI transactions.Going further, SJM called for a ban on US tech and social media companies if Washington pursued what it termed âunilateral economic coercionâ. It asked citizens to begin by boycotting Pepsi, Coke and US-owned social media and e-commerce platforms, saying the campaign could be expanded if American actions continued.The organisation asked the government to reject any attempt to link tariffs with Indiaâs oil purchases and not compromise on agriculture, dairy, energy security or strategic autonomy during trade negotiations.SJM maintained that access to the US market should not be used to force third countries to alter their energy sourcing decisions.

World.title: HC stays Kalyana Lakshmi, Shaadi Mubarak schemes’ operation
World.content:
The Telangana High Court on Wednesday stayed the operation of Kalyana Lakshmi and Shadi Mubarak schemes of the State government till September 9.

Justice N.V. Shravan Kumar of the HC, passing the order in a writ petition filed by advocate Vijay Gopal contending that the two schemes being operated through eight GOs issued by the State government had no legislative or statutory sanction, said the disbursement of money under the schemes to beneficiaries should also be stopped till that date. The petitioner challenged the basis on which the eligibility criteria like the income limit was fixed by the government for enforcement of the two schemes.

The expenditure incurred under the schemes involved substantial amounts from the Consolidated Funds of the State which was contrary to the Articles 202 (3), 204 (3), 266 (3) and 283 (2) of the Constitution of India, the petitioner and advocate Raj Gopal contended. Presenting his contentions, the advocate argued that power to uplift any section of the society must be within the dimension of the legislative power.

As per Article 202, the government had to explain how the public funds were being utilised. He claimed that he had locus standi in the matter under Article 13 (2) to question enforcement of such schemes. The advocate maintained that the State government had not referred to any legislative provisions based on which the two schemes were launched in 2014 and being continued till date. During the previous hearing on August 8, the bench granted time to the government to file counter affidavit answering the issues raised by the petitioner. However, the government counsel on Wednesday further sought time to file the counter affidavit.

World.title: Cauvery: Karnataka will approach Supreme Court, says Cheluvarayaswamy
World.content:
According to Karnataka’s Water Resources Minister, the state is likely to file the plea before Supreme Court on Thursday

Karnataka has decided to approach the Supreme Court against the Cauvery Water Management Authority’s decision on Tuesday to uphold the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee’s (CWRC) direction to the State to release water to Tamil Nadu at a rate of 12,000 cusecs a day for 15 days.

Speaking in New Delhi on Wednesday, Karnataka’s new Water Resources Minister N. Cheluvarayaswamy said, “Karnataka is fully prepared to approach the Supreme Court and I think we may approach the apex court tomorrow (Thursday).”

Mr. Cheluvarayaswamy, who was given the Water Resources portfolio only on Wednesday, said Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Ramalinga Reddy who held the portfolio earlier were in constant touch with the legal and technical team. They had decided to approach the Supreme Court in consultation with these teams, he noted.

Though the earlier order of the CWRC and CWMA asking Karnataka to release water at a rate of 3,500 cusecs a day for 15 days was a difficult one, Karnataka managed to abide by it. “But the present order to ensure flows at a rate of 12,000 cusecs is too difficult to implement as Karnataka would end up releasing roughly 15 tmcft of water,” Mr. Cheluvarayaswamy maintained.

“We need to give priority for drinking water requirements in such a distress situation. The water storage data shows that Tamil Nadu has more storage than Karnataka when drinking water requirements are concerned,” the Minister said.

He said Karnataka needed to conserve drinking water till the beginning of next water year in June 2027 as the weather forecast had indicated that Karnataka was unlikely to get good rains in the remaining part of the monsoon in August and September.

World.title: Kayanad landslips revive safety concerns over abandoned quarries in Ernakulam
World.content:
Back-to-back landslips that occurred at Kayanad near Muvattupuzha amid the recent spell of torrential rain have revived safety concerns over water-filled abandoned quarries, prompting the authorities to initiate steps to allay public fears.

Officials inspected the site after local residents expressed concerns over a suspected water leak from a deep pit formed at one of the abandoned quarries situated upstream of the site where the landslips took place. There are over 30 quarries in the area, which is part of Maradi grama panchayat.

The officials, including disaster management experts, who inspected the area have submitted a preliminary report to the District Collector on the situation at the quarry pond. It is learnt that they have ruled out any immediate danger while suggesting a detailed multi-department inquiry into the suspected safety threat.

“It is not yet ascertained if the landslip downstream had anything to do with the flooding of the abandoned quarry. The suspected seepage from the pit lake has also to be verified. A detailed study by experts, including geologists, may be required before reaching conclusions,” an official said. The authorities, meanwhile, are exploring the possibility of pumping water out of the quarry in a bid to address the concerns of people residing downstream.

The work is likely to be done using funds from the District Mineral Foundation.

A house was damaged and rubber and pineapple farms were inundated in the flash floods caused by landslips that took place near the Shoolam waterfalls at Kayanad last week.

People’s representatives have, meanwhile, called upon the authorities to find out if other abandoned quarries in the district also pose a threat to public safety, especially in the wake of heavy rain causing widespread damage in hilly regions, including Muvattupuzha and Kothamangalam.

“It has to be examined if the water-filled abandoned quarries pose any threat to public safety, and action should be taken accordingly. A comprehensive study has to be conducted on how to make use of the water stored in abandoned quarries productively while ensuring public safety,” district panchayat president K.G. Radhakrishnan said.

The authorities have identified around 80 abandoned quarries in the district as part of measures to ensure safety around the sites in the wake of repeated drowning cases.

World.title: Will not tolerate ‘blackmail’ by rice millers: CM
World.content:
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy has asserted that he will not tolerate any ‘blackmail’ by millers when it comes to collection of dues from them.

He directed the Civil Supplies department officials to formulate a comprehensive policy to collect dues from the rice millers. The Cabinet sub-committee on Civil Supplies should discuss the finer aspects of the issue and evolve guidelines.

He wanted the officials to collect dues from millers who have defaulted in payments and directed them to take over the mills operated by wilful defaulters. The Chief Minister gave these directions during a meeting on Wednesday to review the functioning of the department.

Suggesting appropriate action into the pending dues, he exhorted officials to take steps with an aim to ensure prompt repayments. Options should be explored to entrust the operation of mills of defaulting rice millers to women self-help groups.

Measures should be put in place for optimum utilisation of godowns available in the market, he said asserting that the Government was considering entrustment of milling responsibilities to women groups.

Mr. Reddy wanted the officials to take up a project for construction of godowns spread over 50 to 100 acres in five constituencies on pilot basis. The selection of the constituencies should be based on the quantum of food grain yields so that constituencies with highest yield were selected for construction of godowns. Officials should ensure that foods available under the rural employment guarantee scheme were utilised for the project.

World.title: Putin threatens retaliation for Western seizures of Russian commercial vessels
World.content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) threatened retaliation for Western seizures of its commercial vessels, describing them as “piracy.”

Speaking on a visit to a Russian warship that was taking part in a naval exercise in the Pacific, Mr. Putin described the Western moves to detain vessels linked to Russia as a breach of international maritime law.

“It's nothing but piracy and robbery,” Mr. Putin said. “If this is done, we will be forced to respond in kind.”

He added that the Russian response wouldn't necessarily come in the waters where the Russian ships were seized, noting that Moscow could retaliate “in any area where we see it as necessary and appropriate,” including in the Pacific.

The Pacific Fleet chief, Adm Viktor Liina, reported to Mr. Putin that the navy was ready to start inspections of the commercial ships serving the “unfriendly nations.” He noted that many of the ships operated by British, French and other European carriers fly the flags of other nations, effectively making them a “shadow fleet.”

“We have enough assets for inspection and detention of vessels of the unfriendly nations and their shadow fleet,” Mr. Liina told Mr. Putin. “We are ready to start performing the task.”

Russia is believed to be using a fleet of hundreds of ships to evade international sanctions imposed after Moscow sent troops into Ukraine in February 2022.

France and the U.K. have detained tankers suspected of being of Russia's “shadow fleet” shipping oil in violation of international sanctions. The EU has sanctioned hundreds of “shadow fleet” ships.

Russia has recently started deploying warships to escort its commercial vessels.

Dmitry Medvedev, who served as Russia's President in 2008-2012 to let Mr. Putin observe term limits and is now deputy head of Russia's Security Council, noted that many ships belonging to European carriers fly the so-called “flags of convenience” just like Russian carriers do.

“It means that by applying a symmetrical approach, which is only fair, Russia has the right to attack any merchant vessel belonging to hostile nations, whether in our waters or in neutral waters, provided there are reasonable grounds to suspect it is carrying cargo in the enemy's interest, and that applies to any cargo,” Mr. Medvedev said.

“There are a great many such vessels, and our military is capable of dramatically expanding operations well beyond the Black Sea basin.”

World.title: Govt. approves three H-CITI projects
World.content:
The Telangana government has given a go-ahead to three major road infrastructure projects in Hyderabad under the Engineering Procurement Construction (EPC) mode, at a tender contract value of ₹242.72 crore.

According to the orders issued by the Metropolitan Area & Urban Development Department on Wednesday, the projects comprise construction of a left-arm down ramp for the existing Owaisi Flyover towards Santhosh Nagar, a six-lane bi-directional grade separator from Hafeez Baba Nagar Junction to the 100 Feet Balapur–Church Road Junction, and a six-lane bi-directional flyover at the Bandlaguda-Errakunta crossroad junction.

The government had earlier accorded administrative sanction of ₹339 crore for the works under the Hyderabad City Innovative and Transformative Infrastructure (H-CITI) programme. The GHMC subsequently proposed a revised administrative sanction of ₹385 crore, which included property acquisition component. The civic body was also permitted to invite tenders under the EPC mode, undertake land and property acquisition simultaneously to avoid delays, and engage a Project Management Consultant for supervision, quality control, quality assurance and quality audit.

GHMC invited tenders through the e-procurement platform in January 2026, with an internal benchmark value of ₹231.8725 crore and a contract period of 24 months. KNR Constructions Limited who quoted 4.68% in excess was the sole bidder and was found technically responsive, the orders maintained.

The government has now permitted GHMC to accept the bid, meet the expenditure from the H-CITI head of account and award the works to KNR Constructions Limited after entering into the agreement.

World.title: Civil Surgeon faces probe over alleged use of false caste certificate
World.content:
A Civil Surgeon, who was a resident of Indukurpet mandal in Nellore district, has been facing allegations of obtaining a false Scheduled Caste (SC) certificate around 40 years ago and rising to such a senior position using SC reservations. Upon enquiry, no record was reportedly found indicating that he belongs to the SC community, but rather to the Backward Caste (BC-A).

A case was filed by Peta Chiranjeevi and Peta Vamsidhar in the Andhra Pradesh High Court in July 2022 against Peta Chandrasekhar, who is presently working as Civil Surgeon Specialist (Paediatrician) and in-charge District Coordinator of Hospital Services (DCHS) at Rayachoti Area Hospital in Annamayya district.

As per the Court orders, Nellore Rural Tahsildar conducted an enquiry and ascertained that he belongs to BC-A Jangama community, based on the information given by the villagers of the Kanuparthipadu village. No record was reportedly found indicating that he obtained an SC Beda Jangam community certificate from the then Tahsildar.

Nellore District Collector also reported to Deputy Chief Secretary to Government, Health, Medical and Family Welfare Department, Vijayawada, that Mr. Chandrasekhar had already filed a writ petition in the A.P. High Court along with 131 others seeking SC status to Beda, Budaga Jangama community, and the case was still pending.

“The caste of the Civil Surgeon will be decided only after outcome of the judgement in the writ petition,” Annamayya District Collector Nishant Kumar said in a letter written to A.P. High Court Government Pleader for Social Welfare. He requested to place these facts before the High Court for passing suitable orders in the case.

World.title: Drone helps locate woman lost overnight in Nellore forest
World.content:
A 55-year-old woman lost in a dense forest was traced by the police and Forest department officials using a drone. Nagadasari Ratnamma, a resident of Harijanawada in Obulayapalle village of Rapur mandal in SPSR Nellore district, was found near the Mamidikona base camp on Tuesday (August 11, 2026).

According to the police, she went into the forest to collect firewood on Monday morning around 11 a.m. While returning with the firewood, she lost her way and was stranded, unable to find the path back to the village. She had gone about eight kilometres into the forest, and spent the night under a tree.

Nagadasari Ratnamma, 55, who lost her way while collecting firewood and spent a night in the forest, is brought to safety near the Mamidikona base camp in SPSR Nellore district on Tuesday. The police and Forest Department traced her using a drone.



Video: Special Arrangement pic.twitter.com/gvfh14qkG2 — The Hindu - Andhra Pradesh (@THAndhra) August 12, 2026

Family members and residents searched for her through the night after she failed to return home, but no trace of her was found. They complained to the police the next morning. Rapur Sub-Inspector (SI) Tirumala Rao coordinated a special search involving a drone team, the Mamidikona base camp, the Special Branch police and Forest department officials.

Using the drone alongside information gathered from residents, the search was conducted in the forest. Ratnamma was located on Tuesday morning around 11.30 a.m. and brought out safely. She was taken to the Rapur government hospital for medical examination, after which she was handed over to her husband.

District Superintendent of Police (SP) Ajitha Vejendla commended the Rapur police station staff for their prompt response and coordinated efforts, which helped locate the woman in about three hours. Ratnamma’s family and villagers thanked the police and Forest department personnel for their response.

World.title: After death of 3 Pakistani sailors, FO says Islamabad will implement maritime coalition 'in full earnest'
World.content:
The Foreign Office (FO) said on Wednesday that Pakistan, as a signatory to the recently announced multinational maritime defence coalition, would implement its commitments “in full earnest”.

The statement comes following the deaths of three Pakistani sailors in Houthi strikes on a Saudi cargo ship on Tuesday.

Last month, Riyadh unveiled plans for a multinational maritime defence coalition to protect shipping and energy supply routes in the Red Sea region. Fourteen countries, including Pakistan, Turkiye and Egypt, backed the coalition in a joint statement.

Answering questions at a weekly press briefing, FO spokesperson Tahir Andrabi elaborated that Pakistan was a signatory of the recent joint statement supporting a multinational maritime defence coalition, led by Saudi Arabia, to protect shipping and energy supply routes.

“Pakistan is a signatory to this maritime coalition communique and we will implement it with full earnest,” Andrabi said, adding that the country was engaged with the Saudi authorities in this regard.

Andrabi further said that on the directions of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Pakistan was ascertaining the details of the agreement.

In his opening statement, the FO also said that Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s visit to Iran was aimed at discussing bilateral relations, security-related matters and regional developments, particularly peace and stability in the region.

He said Naqvi — who arrived in Tehran on Tuesday — was holding meetings with senior Iranian officials.

He added that the visit provides the two countries the opportunity to discuss “bilateral relations, security-related matters, and regional development, with a particular focus on efforts to promote peace, stability, and constructive engagement amongst the parties in the region and regional developments”.

Naqvi was received in Tehran by his Iranian counterpart, Eskandar Momeni, and later held talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Iranian media reported.

A diplomatic source had told Dawn from Tehran that the principal objective of Naqvi’s visit was to follow up on the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding and Pakistan’s mediation bet­­w­een Iran and the US.

Speaking further on Pakistan’s mediation efforts between the US and Iran, Andrabi reiterated that Pakistan remained engaged alongside “brotherly states” in “sincere efforts” to work towards a resolution to the crisis.

“Pakistan is making all-out efforts to bring the two parties to the negotiating table and the Islamabad MoU and pave the way for peace and stability in the region,” he said.

He also warned that Pakistan would continue to “offset spoilers using direct and indirect channels” and ensure the continuation of constructive dialogue to resolve outstanding issues.

During the Q&A session, responding to a question regarding the status of the Islamabad MoU, the spokesperson said, “Whenever the rationality for dialogue will overcome the logic of escalation, the template for peace is provided in the Islamabad MoU and Pakistan-Qatar joint statement.”

The current deadline for the 60-day period for US-Iran negotiations under the Islamabad MoU is Aug 17. Andrabi, however, noted that this deadline “can always be extended” if there is the intention to hold dialogue.

“Even then, five days still remain, so we are not closing the chapter,” he added. “But we hope that even if the deadline is not implemented, the extension will take place eventually and the parties will revert to dialogue.”

Asked about the basis for Pakistan’s continued optimism amid the US-Iran conflict, the spokesperson said, “As a mediator and facilitator of talks, we remain optimistic that a solution is in sight.”

He pointed out that during the conflict, the countries had cycled through periods of heightened escalation followed by relative calm and eventual dialogue. He termed this “the natural progression of any armed conflict of international significance”.

“We are not discouraged by escalations, as much as we do not get overly optimistic when there is a period of calm,” he said, while highlighting Pakistan’s sustained engagement with the parties to resolve the conflict.

The country would continue its engagement with optimism “that ought to be there in any credible facilitator and mediator”, he added.

Makkah pact reflects ‘resolve for sharing burden of regional peace’

The FO spokesperson also spoke of the defence pact signed last week between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, which he said was “highlight of the week”.

The joint defence agreement, signed in Makkah on Friday, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

He said the agreement reflected the three nations’ “commitment to further strengthen their collective security, promoting peace security and promoting peace security and stability in the region and beyond”.

He said the agreement reflected the “long-standing brotherly relations” among the three countries and “displays our resolve for sharing the burden of regional peace and security”.

“The agreement is purely defensive in nature and allows unified efforts to confront threats and security challenges to the member states,” Andrabi added, recalling Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar’s statement congratulating the nation on the agreement on August 10, wherein he held the agreement was defensive in nature and not against any country.

Responding to a question, he noted that while the agreement was open to other countries, he was not “particularly aware” of which specific countries may join it in the future. He also said that he was not aware of any consultations with the US and China regarding the agreement, calling this “a matter of diplomatic exchange”, but noted that channels of communication with both countries remained open.

FO rejects Indian MEA’s ‘baseless’ remarks on AJK

When asked about the Indian Ministry of External Affairs’ recent remarks regarding alleged human rights abuses in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), the FO spokesperson rejected the “baseless” statement. The region has been gripped by unrest since early June as elections are also being held.

“India’s professed concerns for human rights in AJK are disingenuous given its own well-documented record for repression in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir, including excessive use of force, arbitrary detention, suppression of political freedom and sweeping powers under the draconian laws enacted there.”

He added that India’s “politicisation” of developments in AJK was “misleading and cannot divert attention from the stark realities in Indian illegally occupied Kashmir”.

“Pakistan remains fully committed to the protection of fundamental rights and the democratic freedom of AJK,” he said.

He added that rather than making such statements over AJK, India would be “well advised to honour commitments made by its founding fathers and uphold the right of the people of Indian illegally occupied Jammu and Kashmir to freely determine their future through a United Nations plebiscite in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions”.

World.title: 18 terrorists killed in Balochistan’s Surab district: ISPR
World.content:
At least 18 terrorists were killed in Balochistan’s Surab district, including eight in a premature detonation, the military’s media wing said on Wednesday.

The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said eight terrorists were killed when an “under preparation” vehicle-borne improvised explosive device (VBIED) detonated.

“An under preparation vehicle-borne improvised explosive device (VBIED) detonated while being prepared by terrorists affiliated with Fitna Al Hindustan in Surab district of Balochistan.”

The state has designated Balochistan-based terrorist groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

The military’s media wing added that multiple terrorists were also injured in the explosion.

However, the blast also killed three civilians in the area after a “secondary detonation of other explosives stored there”.

Following the explosion, a contingent of security forces and police reached the incident site and “launched a comprehensive joint clearance operation to track down the perpetrators and facilitators”.

Elaborating further, the military said security forces “proactively detected the movement of fleeing terrorists, effectively engaging and neutralising ten more”.

“In total, 18 terrorists affiliated with Fitna Al Hindustan have been eliminated in these incidents so far,” said the ISPR, adding that during the exchange of fire, two soldiers were injured.

“Sanitisation operations continue in the area to eliminate any remaining terrorists.

“The relentless counter-terrorism campaign under vision ‘Azm e Istehkam’ (as approved by Federal Apex Committee on National Action Plan) by security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan will continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country,” concluded the ISPR.

Security forces killed 15 terrorists in multiple intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in several areas of Balochistan, state media reported last week.

State-run Pakistan TV, citing sources, reported that the IBOs were carried out in Mastung, Bolan, Washuk, Awaran, Sibi, Khuzdar, Harnai, and Nushki under Operation Raddul Fitna 3, adding that weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the dead terrorists.

“The operations severely damaged the khawarij network and restricted their movement,” Pakistan TV said. Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists.

According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies’ (PICSS) monthly security assessment released on July 31, the security situation deteriorated most significantly in Balochistan in the country last month.

The overall death toll increased by 241pc in Balochistan, from 109 in June to 372 in July, the report said.

Security personnel deaths in Balochistan increased from six in June to 62 in July, representing a rise of 933pc. Terrorist deaths rose from 75 to 238, while civilian deaths increased by 93pc, from 28 to 54. Eighteen members of peace committees were also killed in the province.

World.title: Pakistan ‘still far’ from becoming a social welfare state: PM Shehbaz
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday said that Pakistan was “still far” from becoming a social welfare state, which he said was the original purpose of the country’s formation.

The premier was speaking at an event in Islamabad to mark International Youth Day 2026, observed on August 12.

He also inaugurated several initiatives for the youth, including the Power Sector Innovation Programme, the National Youth Employment Policy and the Skills Ambassador Programme.

As part of the National Youth Employment Policy, the premier announced that a 35 per cent quota would be specified for women in the labour force. Every year, a 10pc quota will be specified for startups as well to facilitate youth in starting their own businesses, he said.

In his speech, PM Shehbaz said that Daanish schools were a step towards making Pakistan a country where young people would have equal opportunities for advancement, irrespective of their financial status.

He said that during his tenure as Punjab chief minister, he had established Daanish schools to improve access to quality education for the poor.

“How unfortunate is it that, on the one hand, there is a Pakistan for the children of the elite, who not only receive the best education in Pakistan but also attend the best international institutions in the UK and North America?

“Contrastingly, there is another Pakistan where millions of parents’ children, who desperately want an education, are not provided even basic educational opportunities.”

Today, thousands of graduates of Daanish schools are doctors, engineers and teachers, he said. The PM said that progress being achieved through Daanish schools was a realisation of the dream that Quaid-i-Azam had for Pakistan.

Addressing the Daanish school students present in the audience, he said, “the largest part of Pakistan’s population is you. And if we could not give you essential skills, then we won’t be forgiven in this world or the next.”

PM Shehbaz mentioned that in this year’s budget, an amount has also been specified for youth empowerment and development.

Like last year, 1,000 high-achieving students will be sent to China this year for agriculture education, the premier said. He announced that in addition, this year, high-achieving students would be given a state-funded opportunity to study IT and AI in China.

He also announced the establishment of what he described as “Pakistan’s top university”, to be named Daanish University, which would focus on technology education.

Education at Daanish University will be provided free of cost and will be based only on merit, the premier said.

PM Shehbaz added that 250,000 high-achieving students would be awarded Chromebook laptops this year.

He commented that his laptop scheme, when it was first started in Punjab, was criticised but, he added, the programme has allowed the youth to gain advancement opportunities.

“Today, I, in front of the youth, promise that until Allah has given me the responsibility to serve the nation, I will do everything in my power for your prosperity and employment.”

“Our ancestors built Pakistan in 1947, and the Pakistan of 2047 will be built by your vision and energy,” the premier told the students attending the event.

Chairman of the Prime Minister’s Youth Programme Rana Mashhood Ahmed Khan also spoke at the event, where he said, “We work day and night for our youth.”

He praised PM Shehbaz for providing opportunities for the youth during his tenure as chief minister of Punjab and commended the premier’s leadership in advancing Pakistan, adding that under his leadership, no one could stop the country from moving forward.

“The world is talking about Pakistan’s progress today,” he said.

World.title: Met Office forecasts fresh rain spell for upper, central parts of country from Aug 13-15
World.content:
The upper and central parts of the country are set to receive a fresh spell of monsoon rains from August 13 to 15, the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) said on Wednesday.

In an advisory, the Met Office said monsoon currents were penetrating the upper parts of the country along with a westerly wave.

In Kashmir, it forecast rain accompanied by wind and thundershowers in Neelum Valley, Muzaffarabad, Rawalakot, Poonch, Hattian, Bagh, Haveli, Sudhanoti, Kotli, Bhimber and Mirpur. In Gilgit-Baltistan, the Met Office predicted rain in Diamir, Astore, Ghizer, Skardu, Hunza, Gilgit, Ghanche and Shigar.

In upper Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), Dir, Chitral, Swat, Kohistan, Malakand, Shangla, Battagram, Mansehra, Abbottabad, Galiyat, Buner, Bajaur, Mohmand, Peshawar, Nowshera, Mardan, Swabi, Haripur, Kurram and Khyber are expected to receive rain.

In northeast Punjab, rainfall was predicted in Murree, Sialkot, Narowal, Mandi Bahauddin, Gujrat, Gujranwala, Hafizabad, Wazirabad, Lahore, Kasur, Sheikhupura and Nankana Sahib from the night of August 12 to August 15, with occasional gaps.

Rain-wind and thundershowers, with a few heavy falls, are also expected in Islamabad, Rawalpindi and the Pothohar region from the night of August 13 to August 15, with occasional gaps.

In Sargodha, Faisalabad, Jhang, Toba Tek Singh, Khushab, Layyah, Bhakkar, Noorpur Thal, Sahiwal, Pakpattan, Bahawalnagar, Bahawalpur, Dera Ghazi Khan, Zhob, Barkhan and Musakhel, the Met Office predicted rainfall from August 12 to 15.

Meanwhile, in Sindh, partly cloudy to cloudy weather is expected in the southeastern and coastal areas, with chances of rain-wind/thundershowers in Tharparkar, Umerkot and Sanghar districts on August 12 and 13.

Elsewhere in Sindh, hot and humid weather is expected to persist.

The Met Office warned of urban flooding in low-lying areas of Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Mardan, Swabi, Gujranwala, Gujrat, Sialkot and Lahore during the forecast period.

It also indicated the possibility of landslides in vulnerable areas of upper KP, including Dir, Chitral, Swat, Kohistan, Buner, Battagram, Mansehra, Haripur and Abbottabad, as well as in GB, Murree, Galiyat and Kashmir.

The Met Office advised tourists to exercise caution, while farmers were urged to manage crop activities in accordance with weather conditions.

According to the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), 155 people have lost their lives and 460 have been injured in rain-related incidents in the current monsoon season.

Monsoon rains fall across the region from June to September, offering respite from the summer heat and are crucial to replenishing water supplies.

However, heavy downpours also trigger deadly floods, landslides and displacement, particularly in vulnerable, poorly drained, or densely populated areas.

World.title: California Senate unanimously backs stronger Pakistan-US ties
World.content:
WASHINGTON: The California State Senate has unanimously passed a resolution celebrating the “enduring relationship” between Pakistan and the United States and recognising the “significant contributions” of Pakistani-Americans to the state’s economy, culture and social fabric.

The resolution, presented by Senator Melissa Hurtado, highlighted the “pivotal role” played by Pakistani-Americans in California and commended their achievements across diverse fields. It also urged all Californians to join in celebrating the friendly relations between the two countries.

The resolution’s language goes beyond a routine recognition of the Pakistani-American community, placing its contributions alongside California’s relationship with Pakistan and calling for broader public recognition of the friendship between the two countries.

Pakistan’s Ambassador to the United States, Rizwan Saeed Sheikh, also visited California during this process and held meetings with state lawmakers to expand political and economic engagement between Pakistan and the state.

The California State Assembly also adopted a resolution supporting stronger relations with Pakistan. It called for promoting the role of Pakistani-American businesses and investors in advancing economic cooperation between Pakistan and California.

Ambassador Sheikh welcomed the Senate resolution and praised Senator Hurtado for her leadership. He said that Pakistan remained committed to “deepening people-to-people ties” and building on what he described as the “current positive trajectory” in Pakistan-US relations.

The ambassador also held talks with Senator Eloise Gomez on expanding trade, investment and economic cooperation between Pakistan and the United States. Gomez praised Pakistan’s role in promoting regional peace and stability, while Sheikh invited her to visit Pakistan.

He later hosted a working lunch for Assembly member Matt Haney and Assemblywoman Sharon Quirk-Silva. The discussions covered bilateral cooperation, with the ambassador inviting both lawmakers to visit Pakistan.

The Council of Pakistan, led by Dr Imran Sharief, also played a role in efforts leading to the passage of the Senate resolution.

The California resolutions come at a time when Pakistan is seeking to strengthen economic and political engagement with the United States while expanding ties with individual US states.

For Pakistan, the California initiative is significant not only because of its explicit celebration of the “enduring relationship” between the two countries, but also because it widens the role of the Pakistani-American community in expanding political and economic ties between Pakistan and the United States.

World.title: Norwegian FM to visit Pakistan on Aug 13-14, first such visit in a decade
World.content:
Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide will undertake an official visit to Pakistan on August 13-14 to discuss avenues for expanding bilateral cooperation, trade and investment.

In a statement, the Foreign Office (FO) said, “At the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Norwegian FM Eide will undertake an official visit to Pakistan on 13-14 August 2026.”

According to the FO, the visit to Pakistan will be the first by a Norwegian foreign minister in a decade.

During the visit, the FO said that Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and his Norwegian counterpart would hold delegation-level talks covering the full spectrum of Pakistan-Norway relations.

“The two sides will discuss avenues for further expanding bilateral cooperation, particularly in trade and investment, climate change, renewable energy, education and people-to-people contacts.

“They will also exchange views on important regional and international developments,” it added.

FM Eide has appreciated and acknowledged Pakistan’s efforts to de-escalate tensions in the region through mediation during the US-Israeli war on Iran.

The FO stated that the visit would provide an opportunity to “further strengthen the longstanding and cordial relations between Pakistan and Norway and to explore new areas of mutually beneficial cooperation”.

During his visit to Norway in May, FM Dar also had a meeting with Norwegian deputy foreign minister and discussed the regional situation with him.

World.title: Millions of people in Iceland and Spain set for 'event of the century' eclipse
World.content:
Millions of people gathered in Iceland and northern Spain to witness Europe’s first total solar eclipse in 27 years on Wednesday, with Spanish officials warning people to avoid areas where a heatwave has raised the risk of wildfires.

Authorities were expecting up to 6 million visitors in mostly rural areas within the eclipse’s path across the north of Spain and the Balearic Islands, said Juan Cruz, Spain’s Secretary of State for Science.

“I hope that tonight will see the emergence of a wonderful generation of astrophysicists,” he said. “It’s such a special moment.” The eclipse will be quickly followed by the sunset in Spain, making the event particularly alluring.

Police, planes, and helicopters are on standby

The uncanny sensation when day briefly turns into twilight and some animals fall quiet as the moon passes directly between Earth and the Sun was often treated as an omen in the past, a cosmic struggle or a sign of divine power.

Frenchman Leyssalle Anthony, 39, prepares a telescope to view the total solar eclipse from the beach, in Arija, Spain, August 12, 2026. — Reuters

Now, Spain sees it as a chance to showcase seldom-visited regions and draw tourists away from its overcrowded beach resorts, while also rolling out a massive police operation and public safety campaign to prevent them from causing wildfires.

Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska told reporters 25,000 police officers had been assigned to guarantee security around the eclipse observation while nearly 100 planes and helicopters were also being deployed.

He called on citizens to follow the eclipse from the hundreds of observation points set up by authorities and abide by the restrictions set up around some parks. “Let’s not forget that the wildfire risk is very high; it’s extreme due to high temperatures,” he said.

Lola Guerreiro spent the night in the mountains near Arco de las Salinas in eastern Spain, home to Galactica Europe’s largest educational astronomy centre as well as the Javalambre observatory, after making the long drive from Extremadura to view the eclipse.

People walk out of a portable planetarium during an eclipse watch party on the day of a total solar eclipse in Buitrago del Lozoya, Spain, August 12, 2026. — Reuters

“Watching a total solar eclipse has been a dream of mine for many, many years, and I didn’t want to miss the chance to experience it, even though it meant a seven-hour journey,” she said.

Sergio, a 60-year-old Italian, had made the trek in a camping van with his family to Arija in northern Spain.

“I do feel a little emotional. Yes, because I know I won’t have another chance in my life to see an eclipse, a phenomenon like this,” he said.

The Iberian Peninsula last saw a total solar eclipse in 1912. It is set to experience another one on August 2, 2027, and an annular eclipse in January 2028, completing the so-called “Iberian Eclipse Trio.”

Eclipse fever in the land of sagas

In Iceland’s capital Reykjavik, glasses to allow people to look at the phenomenon without damaging their eyes have been sold out for days as the Nordic country of roughly 400,000 people expects to welcome up to 80,000 visitors.

A narrow path of totality will reach Iceland’s westernmost coast at about 5:44pm (1744 GMT), before the moon’s shadow races east.

People lie down inside a portable planetarium during an eclipse watch party on the day of a total solar eclipse in Buitrago del Lozoya, Spain, August 12, 2026. — Reuters

Totality will last up to 2 minutes and 13 seconds in the far west, though most cities will see shorter periods of darkness. Authorities have warned of heavy traffic and urged viewers to arrive early.

Singer Bjork was due to perform a DJ set at an eclipse-themed event south of Reykjavik.

US space agency Nasa plans to fly a high-altitude WB-57 aircraft from Iceland to follow the moon’s shadow, and Nasa-funded teams will launch balloons to study how the sudden darkness and cooling affect the lower atmosphere.

“This is a once-in-a-lifetime experience,” said Karen Williams, 51, who was visiting from Britain. “I love the outdoors, and so I wanted to come and see the eclipse and just experience it.”

Angela Cordoba reacts as she wears virtual reality goggles next to her grandchildren, Gadea, 3, and Giulia, 6, as they attend an eclipse watch party on the day of a total solar eclipse in Buitrago del Lozoya, Spain, August 12, 2026.

“Although I do hear, probably in the UK where I’ve come from… they’re going to get a better view of it than us here tonight.” Skies over Iceland were overcast on Wednesday with the Icelandic Met office predicting clouds and rain for much of the path of the eclipse, adding that the best chances of breaks in the solid cover were expected in the northwest of the country.

Aside from casual observers, the event also draws “eclipse chasers”, enthusiasts who crisscross the globe to be in the path of totality whenever an eclipse occurs.

Gordon Telepun, a retired plastic surgeon and amateur astronomer from the US who has photographed six total eclipses, said he would watch from the island of Mallorca because Spain checked all the boxes for eclipse chasers.

World.title: Former Chinese premier Zhu Rongji dies aged 97
World.content:
Former Chinese premier Zhu Rongji, whose market reforms helped drive the country’s extraordinary economic rise, died on Wednesday at the age of 97.

Zhu became premier in 1998 and swiftly lived up to his reputation as a hard-hitting free marketeer. Among his best-known reforms were a broad programme to privatise unprofitable state-owned enterprises, the privatisation of urban housing and the promotion of home ownership.

He passed away from illness in Beijing late Wednesday morning “after medical treatment failed to save him”, state news agency Xinhua reported.

“The life of comrade Zhu Rongji was a life of revolution, a life of struggle, a life of glory,” an obituary jointly issued by China’s top political bodies said, according to Xinhua.

“It was a life dedicated wholeheartedly to serving the people, one given to the communist cause. His passing is a major loss for the Party and the country.”

Reforms under Zhu sparked a boom in real estate and construction, which would soar to become a quarter of China’s economy before a crippling debt crisis struck in 2020.

His leadership was credited with helping China avoid the worst of the 1997 Asian financial crisis, bucking a global trend.

He also led negotiations for China’s accession to the World Trade Organisation in 2001 — a move seen as consolidating the country’s transformation from an isolated economy under Mao Zedong to the marketplace of the world.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took to X to express his condolences to Xi, sitting Chinese Premier Li Qiang, Zhu’s family and the Chinese public.

“Deeply saddened by the passing of former Chinese premier Zhu Rongji, a great leader and a good friend of Pakistan,” he wrote. “Pakistan shares the grief of our iron brother China at this sad hour.”

Zhu was “an outstanding member of the Communist Party of China, a long-tested and loyal communist fighter … [and] an outstanding leader of the Party and the state”, his obituary said.

But Zhu’s brand of market reformism, which lifted millions out of poverty but unleashed inequality, fell out of vogue with the ascent of Xi Jinping in 2012.

Xi has condemned runaway capitalism and sought to move China onto a more balanced development path, as well as cracking down on excessive displays of wealth and private firms seen as monopolistic.

Elderly men talk next to a giant screen broadcasting a portrait of late former Chinese Premier Zhu Rongji, in Beijing, China on August 12, 2026. — Reuters

“We must turn our grief into strength, learn from [Zhu’s] revolutionary spirit, noble character and fine conduct, and rally even more closely around the Party Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core,” the obituary read.

News of his death quickly shot to the top trending on social media platform Weibo, with the topic gaining more than 190 million views just hours after it was announced.

“The people’s good premier, go in peace,” read one comment under the news on Weibo with more than 17,000 likes.

Others left candle emojis in remembrance.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent. These should be reduced to zero percent for renewable energy expansion.

The third reform is a tax holiday. Rooftop solar power producers and project companies should receive benefits comparable to those of utility-scale renewable energy producers. A practical structure could be a 100 percent tax holiday for the first 10 years, 50 percent for the next 3 years, and 25 percent for the next 2 years. This should apply to CAPEX, OPEX, IPP, and MPP models. A broader 10–20 year tax holiday for renewable energy projects should also be considered.

Bangladesh has a remarkable solar opportunity already waiting on its rooftops. About 7 percent of the country’s land is covered with concrete or other built structures. This means more than 10,000 square kilometres, or about 10 billion square meters of built surface. If only 30 percent is usable, that would give around 3 billion square meters. At 10 square meters per kW, this can create nearly 300 GW of solar potential. Bangladesh’s peak demand is only around 16–18 GW. The opportunity already exists on rooftops, factories, warehouses, schools, hospitals, government buildings, and commercial establishments.

Rooftop solar should therefore be relaunched nationwide with a clear business model. Utility-scale solar also needs support through unused khas land, transparent tendering, and grid readiness. Floating solar, river-based solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage should receive separate policy attention.

The suspended solar projects must also be revisited. A total of 31 solar power projects, with a combined capacity of more than 3,000 MW, were previously suspended or cancelled. Many were being developed by foreign investors, with more than USD 200 million reportedly already invested. If implemented, these projects could save around BDT 10,800 crore annually in energy import costs. They should be reassessed and revived quickly.

Energy storage is another missing pillar. Solar and wind need storage support to become more reliable. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and other storage systems should be reduced to zero. This will help stabilise renewable power and support future grid flexibility.

Electric vehicles can also become part of the solution. In China, Japan, and the United States, EVs are increasingly seen as mobile energy storage systems. A typical EV battery has a capacity of 40–70 kWh, enough to power an average household for 1–2 days. If Bangladesh had 1 million EVs, the country would have 40–70 GWh of distributed storage. This is several times higher than the daily peak demand gap. Solar-powered EV charging, vehicle-to-home, and vehicle-to-grid systems should be included in future energy planning.

If Bangladesh had 30–40 percent of the grid powered by solar, along with solar-powered EVs, the country would be far less exposed to global fuel market shocks. Long fuel lines, online schooling, shorter office hours, and industrial disruption could be reduced. Solar, storage, and EVs should now be planned together.

Finance will decide how fast this transition happens. Renewable energy projects cannot grow at interest rates below 10–12 percent. Long-term financing should be available at an interest rate of 3.5–4.5 percent. A 10–15-year financing facility at a maximum interest rate of 5 percent should be introduced. Bangladesh Bank’s green refinancing fund should be expanded. Rooftop and residential solar customers should be eligible for collateral-free loans. The LC margin for renewable equipment should be limited to 5%.

Net metering must be simplified. Approval should be completed within 15–30 days through a one-stop service. Approval, interconnection, inspection, billing adjustment, and utility coordination should all be simple and time-bound. Wheeling charges for renewable energy should also be kept reasonable and low. The Merchant Power Policy should be clear, simple, and investment-friendly so that industries and commercial consumers can directly procure renewable electricity.

Agriculture should also be included in the solar transition. Bangladesh can set a target to convert 1.5 million diesel irrigation pumps into solar pumps. This will reduce diesel imports, lower farmers’ production costs, and protect the environment. The program should include duty-free facilities, low-cost loans, investment support, and local service networks.

Waste-to-energy should also receive policy support. City corporations need clear rules, easy financing, and private-sector participation to enable urban waste management and distributed power generation to work together.

Bangladesh now needs a phased national roadmap for renewable energy.

In the short term, within 0–6 months, customs duty, VAT, and taxes on renewable energy equipment should be reduced to zero. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and energy storage should be withdrawn. Approval for net metering should be obtained within 15–30 days. Industrial and commercial solar installations should be eligible for special incentives. The 31 suspended solar projects should be reassessed. Wheeling charges should be rationalised. Solar, storage, and EV charging should receive urgent policy support. Collateral-free lines of credit should be introduced for rooftop solar. NBR should quickly implement assessment reform and a 0 percent duty.

In the medium term, within 1–3 years, renewable energy financing should be available at a maximum interest rate of 5 percent for 10–15 years. The LC margin should be limited to 5 percent. Land banks and grid infrastructure should be developed for utility-scale solar. Merchant Power Policy and MPPA should be simplified. Rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, and hybrid solar-storage projects should receive a 10–15-year tax holiday. A national program should convert 1.5 million diesel pumps into solar pumps. Rooftop solar should be made mandatory or incentive-based for government buildings, industrial zones, EPZs, economic zones, and large commercial buildings. EV solar charging and distributed storage policies should be developed. Renewable energy skill development and employment programs should also be launched.

In the long term, within 3–10 years, Bangladesh should aim to reach more than 10,000 MW of solar power by 2030. Offshore and onshore wind should be developed. Floating solar, river-based solar, and agrivoltaics should be implemented. A National Energy Storage Strategy should be prepared. Smart grid and power sector digitalisation should be accelerated. Local assembly and manufacturing of solar panels, inverters, mounting structures, battery packs, BMS, and EV charging equipment should be encouraged. Regional power trade should be expanded. The Renewable Purchase Obligation should be introduced. Fossil fuel subsidies should be gradually redirected to a renewable energy transition fund.

Image Visual: Anwar Sohel

The benefits can be large. Energy import costs will fall. Pressure on foreign currency reserves will decline. Industrial production costs will reduce. Export competitiveness will improve. The subsidy burden will decrease. New investment will grow. Renewable energy can create 20–25 jobs per MW through rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, solar pumps, EV charging, battery storage, smart grids, manufacturing, installation, operation, and maintenance.

The government may worry about revenue loss from tax and duty exemptions. But this should be seen as an investment. In the short term, there may be a limited impact on revenue. In the long term, Bangladesh can save far more by reducing fuel imports, lowering subsidies, saving foreign currency, strengthening industries, and attracting new investment.

Bangladesh’s energy crisis is a major challenge but also a historic opportunity. The crisis is not only a supply problem. It is a policy framework problem. Renewable energy, especially solar power, storage, and EV integration, can be among the most practical solutions for the country.

The question is no longer whether Bangladesh should adopt renewable energy. The real question is how quickly, how systematically, and how boldly the country can complete this transition.



Mohammad Ataur Rahman Sarker is a renewable energy entrepreneur and the secretary of the Bangladesh Sustainable and Renewable Energy Association.

Md. Tanvir Siraj is a renewable energy researcher.

World.title: The forgotten art of Bengali advertising
World.content:
I have never seen someone at a rustic village market, anklets jingling, shouting slogans for "Khol Company’s Ringworm Ointment." No smooth-talker has ever leaned in, fanning out thin booklets like a deck of cards, whispering rhythmically, "Here are the mysteries of Gopal Bhar, and here—the secret love letters."

I never hid colourful s of a reclining Gauhar Jaan, cigarette in hand, between the folds of shirts in my drawer. I did indeed rummage through my grandfather’s pockets to collect old tram tickets, but none of them bore that curious notice for "Ashtavakra Toothpowder."
